items.title: Recipe layer: composable project recipes mined from real implementations
items.body:
## The gap

The plugin makes Claude a good *assistant* — one scoped question, one hook, one query. It cannot
**build a project**. Ask it to "set up AP invoice processing into an ERP" and it has every ingredient
and no recipe: it does not know which extensions run in which order, what must exist before matching
works, or what a finished implementation looks like.

That missing knowledge is **assembly**: order, dependency, integration. #88 / #86 add the layer of
**parts** (parameterized fragments with their traps written down). This issue is the layer above: the
plan that assembles parts into a working implementation.

**Naming: decided — `recipes/`, each file a recipe** (e.g. `ap-invoice-to-erp`). Parts are
ingredients; a recipe is the ordered assembly. `architectures/` was rejected because #86 took
`blueprints` and the two share a metaphor; `recipes/` is the only candidate where **ordering is
inherent to the word**, which matters because silent ordering errors are the highest-value knowledge
this layer carries. Precedent: Chef cookbooks, Yocto recipes.

## What a recipe is

Not more config — a thin, ordered, checkable plan that *references* parts:

```json
{
  "recipe": "ap-invoice-to-erp",
  "shape": { "document": "ap-invoice", "target": "rest-erp", "master_data": ["vendor","po","gl"] },
  "hook_chain": {
    "annotation_content.initialize": [
      { "part": "capture-page-text-to-field", "why_here": "reasoning fields need text parked first" },
      { "part": "mdh-exact-to-fuzzy-cascade", "binds": {"dataset": "<vendor collection>"},
        "requires": {"sideload": ["schemas"], "token_owner": "hook"} }
    ],
    "export": [ { "part": "export-oauth-token-cache" }, { "part": "export-create-upload-submit" } ]
  },
  "phases": [
    { "phase": "matching", "goal": "vendor + PO resolved",
      "decide": ["Atlas index on the vendor collection? (no index → fuzzy returns zero rows silently)"],
      "verify": "match rate on 20 real documents > 80%" },
    { "phase": "validation", "goal": "bad data blocks automation",
      "gap": "no parts exist yet — build from business-rules-reference" }
  ],
  "field_flow": [ { "from": "mdh-cascade.matched_id", "to": "export-submit.vendor_ref" } ]
}
```

Five things this carries that no current artifact does:

1. **`hook_chain` — order per event, with the reason.** Ordering errors are *silent*: a hook that runs
   before the field it reads is populated reads empty and writes nothing.
2. **`decide` — the branch points** an SA resolves per customer, stated up front.
3. **`verify` — the exit test per phase.** Turns "built" into "proven" and gives Claude a stopping
   condition.
4. **`field_flow` — the wiring**, so a chain can be machine-checked for "step 4 reads a field nobody
   wrote".
5. **`gap` — honest holes**, which also generate the parts backlog.

## Library recipe vs worked recipe

| | **Library recipe** | **Worked recipe** |
|---|---|---|
| What | Canonical pattern mined from ≥5 implementations | One customer's plan, derived from it |
| Contains | Field *families*, `decide` questions, part refs | Real collection names, schema ids, answers |
| Lives in | `recipes/` here (public) | That customer's `prd2` project |
| Reusable | Yes — the point | No, by definition |

**A worked recipe must never come back into this repo.** Instantiating a recipe means putting customer
specifics into it, so a worked recipe is customer data by construction. Wants a CI guard, not a
convention: fail when any file under `recipes/` contains `resolved_decisions`, or a `binds` value that
is not a `<placeholder>`.

## What gets published

**We publish how hooks connect and how data flows between them — never who it was built for.** A
recipe is event order, part references, decision questions, field *families* and verification
criteria. That is the whole artifact.

The care is one step upstream: mining means pulling real `prd2` trees, and those contain org ids,
hostnames, collection names and secret references.

- **Private tier** — raw pulls, shape records, cluster analysis, SOW-derived intent. Never here.
- **Public tier** (`recipes/`) — generalized structure only.

Never-list for the extractor: org names/ids, queue/hook/schema ids, customer field values, document
content, SOW prose, collection *contents*, endpoint hostnames, credential references. PR #86 is the
cautionary precedent — two client references reached a `provenance` string in a hand-written library.

Two rules follow: **`provenance` is a count, not a list** (`"derived from 7 implementations"`), and
**n≥5 per cluster before publishing** — a recipe built from one or two implementations is a description
of that customer's system, recognisable to them even with names stripped.

## Census (2026-08-18): one family, two variants

24 local implementations, 21 AP invoice (88%). Two findings changed the design.

**One recipe family, two variants, keyed on integration shape** — what the implementation *does*, not
the extension that implements it. `https_out` n=10; `file_out` n=12; 4 do both, 6 neither. Both clear
n≥5.

Crucially, **Request Processor and the older per-call REST chain are the same integration shape** —
synchronous HTTPS out, multi-call, response-chained. One is eight hooks, the other one hook with four
stages. That is *packaging*, not architecture, so a recipe must not fork on it: `legacy_rest_chain`
n=10, `request_processor` n=2 (both in the same two trees — a migration in progress). Carried by
`status`, never by splitting the recipe.

Two by-products: `custom_format_template` appears in 14 trees across both shapes, so it is a shared
**part**, not a recipe axis; and 4 of 21 AP trees have no classifiable export mechanism, so the
extractor must emit **`unclassified`** rather than snap to the nearest known pattern.

One classifier rule, learned the hard way: **classify packaging from hook `settings` keys, never from
endpoint hostnames** (`stages` ⇒ request processor, `request`+`auth` ⇒ legacy chain, `export_configs`
⇒ payload build). The census keyed on hostnames and mislabelled a tree.

**Mining encodes the past, so a recipe needs `status`.** The modal packaging is the shape we would
*not* choose for new work; prevalence is evidence of history, not desirability.

- `status: preferred` — what new work should reach for.
- `status: supported` — widely deployed, fully valid, carries `preferred_alternative`.

**`supported` is not deprecation.** A project can have sound reasons to stay: a hard migration blocker
(an export chain relying on a formula evaluating *between* hooks cannot collapse into one hook, since
formulas only evaluate after a hook completes), a stable production export, or target constraints. So
the rule is narrow: mining must not *elect* a shape preferred by count. A mined pattern lands as
`supported` by default; promotion is explicit human judgement. Where the choice is per-project it
belongs in `decide[]`, not in `status`.

## Target profile drives structure

An earlier revision demoted target vendor to a `binds` seam on the strength of 58% of export
endpoints being unclassifiable. That generalised from the **export** leg alone and is wrong for the
implementation as a whole.

Inbound, the target determines whole hooks and collections. Across trees targeting one major
procurement platform: `{supplier, purchase_order}` 8 of 8, `+ tax_code` 7 of 8, `+ address` 6 of 8. A
tree targeting a different ERP imports `{cost_center, gl_account, po, tax_code}` — a different role
set, not less of the same one.

So a target is a **leaf detail outbound** (hostname, auth, payload names — a genuine seam) and a
**structural driver inbound**. `target_profile` joins the shape record:

```
name_class:        coupa | sap | netsuite | oracle | custom_erp | middleware | unknown
md_inbound_roles:  [supplier, purchase_order, address, tax_code, cost_center, gl_account, ...]
coding_dimensions: [cost_center, gl_account, wbs, project, business_unit]
hop:               direct | middleware
```

`name_class` is orientation only — **clustering keys on the characteristics, never the name.**

**And a recipe that describes only the export leg describes the minority of the work.** Import hooks
outnumber export hooks in 20 of 24 trees (27 vs 12, 36 vs 12, 52 vs 33, 68 vs 39). `hook_chain` must
cover the scheduled/manual import events, and `phases` needs a **master-data** phase ahead of
matching, with its own `verify` — matching cannot work before it passes.

## Operating the layer: match, deviate, contribute

**1. Match — works from the first recipe onward.** Run the extractor over one pulled tree, produce its
shape record, compare against published recipes: *follows recipe X (variant V)* / *follows X with
deviations* / *matches nothing*. This is the read path and it pays out earliest — `analyze` and
`document` can consume it as soon as one recipe exists.

**2. Deviate — the deviation report is the point.** "This project follows `ap-invoice-export` but its
matching stage runs after validation and it has no export guard" is a review finding no current skill
can produce, because no artifact knows what the shape was *supposed* to be. A deviation seen once is a
finding; the same deviation five times is a variant.

**3. Contribute — incremental by design.** A novel shape becomes a shape record plus a **candidate**.
Pulling a new project always adds evidence and can tip a candidate over the threshold, but cannot
publish a recipe by itself.

## Where it comes from

Not authored from memory — **extracted**, so the shapes reflect what ships.

- **A. Config** — `prd2` pulls (queues, schemas, hooks + events/order, rules, datasets, export config).
- **B. Intent** — the SOW for each: what the customer *ordered*. Connects to #87.
- **C. Outcome** — per-queue automation rate, so a recipe carries evidence rather than opinion.

Pipeline: **normalize** each tree into a *shape record* → **cluster** by (document type × target
profile × integration shape) → **join** intent → shape → outcome → **generalize** everything
customer-specific into a seam, a `decide`, or a variant. The join carries an **observed range, never a
point estimate**; any illustrative number must be marked illustrative.

## Deliverables

- `recipes/<name>/recipe.json` + `README.md` (the narrative an SA reads)
- `recipes/README.md` — the contract, including the `status` rule
- `hook-ordering.md` — cross-recipe ordering rules (standalone value before any recipe is complete)
- a **matcher** — nearest recipe + deviations + `unclassified` when nothing fits
- a `recipe-index` autoload pack, guarded against the filesystem
- `implement` wired to it (today its SKILL.md mentions parts 0 times)
- CI guards: every `part` reference resolves; `field_flow` is closed; `gap` markers have a backlog
  issue; index matches filesystem; a `verified_against` staleness stamp; and no worked recipe under
  `recipes/`

## Phasing — each phase has an exit test

- **Census** — done, see above.
- **P0 — validate the record shape on 5 implementations by hand.** Exit: two readers independently
  produce the same record. **Done — see the result comment.** The binding constraint turned out to be
  the schema, not reader agreement.
- **P1 — tracer recipe end to end.** Hand-author from the shape records plus expert review, *before*
  any extractor. Exit: Claude builds a working implementation in a sandbox from the recipe alone and
  each phase's `verify` passes. **Done — see the result comment.**
- **P2 — extractor script** (stdlib, reads a local tree, no API calls). Exit: reproduces the hand-made
  records.
- **P3 — full corpus + clustering.** Exit: clusters confirm or correct the census. **Stop here if they
  do not hold** — that is itself worth knowing.
- **P4 — mined upgrade + next recipes.** Provenance becomes a count; publish every cluster with n≥5.
- **P5 — SOW join** (#87 overlap) and outcome ranges. Exit: given an anonymized SOW excerpt, Claude
  proposes the right recipe and names what it cannot resolve.

## Depends on #86

1. `produces`/`consumes` must resolve to **real schema ids after params are filled**, or `field_flow`
   cannot be checked and recipes degrade to prose.
2. Parts must be readable via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, or Claude can follow a recipe on a customer
   project and still not open the parts it names.

## Open questions

- Does a worked recipe get a formal schema, or is it a library recipe with the seams closed?
- Where does the private corpus live — private repo, or private branch/submodule?
- Does the SOW join need Legal/DPA sign-off before intent categories are extracted, even privately?
- Do variants live inside one recipe file or as siblings?
- Who owns promotion from `supported` to `preferred`, and does it need a second reviewer?
- `position_group` vs `instances` both describe "several hooks at one position" — settle before the
  extractor encodes one reading.

<sub>Design drafted with Claude Code. Related: #88 / #86 (parts layer below), #87 (write-sow → intent),
#44 (feedback loop → gap capture).</sub>

items.title: Synthetic data: seed 42, held-out seed 43 and planted ground truth
items.body:
Product line: Demo v1: Signal Engine | Depends on: #1 to integrate (spec and code-only steps start beside it); #14 before the generation step | Run by: L1 orchestrator, one codex worker | Estimate: 2.0 h agent time | Crown-jewel: no

## User value

After this, the repo holds realistic exports from seven tools for fictional insurers with a known answer planted in them, plus a smaller held-out set nobody tunes on, so every later stage is scored against ground truth instead of impressions, and a reader can check the pipeline was not tuned to one dataset.

## Context

- Read first: docs/data.md in full (sections 4 to 9 are the specification); docs/evals.md sections 4.1 to 4.4 (how ground truth is matched; the held-out and stability suites); docs/architecture.md section 4 (ranking formula, for the probe) and section 11 (`generate` flags); docs/research/datasets-and-source-schemas.md (field names).
- Where this issue and docs/data.md differ, this issue wins: it carries the review rulings data.md may not show yet.
- Files this issue owns: generator/** (spec/*.yaml, spec/holdout/*.yaml, prompts/, cache/, cli.py; build/ is git-ignored), data/raw/**, data/ground_truth.yaml, data/holdout/**, config/teams.yaml, tests/test_generator*.py, tests/test_leaks.py. You may reword descriptions in config/taxonomy.yaml (owned by #1) only if the leak test hits them; flag it at the top of the PR.
- Uses from #1: the gateway (chat with `cache_dir=generator/cache`, stage `generate`; no model_call rows, the generator is not a pipeline run), contracts/sources/*.schema.json, the `generate` slot (`generator.cli:main(argv)`).
- Start at once on the spec files, the prompt and the plan, assemble and verify code with their own tests; rebase onto main when #1 merges, then wire the gateway.

## Done means

- [ ] `uv run keelwater generate --seed 42 --dry-run` makes no model calls and prints the plan: records per source as in data.md section 5 (Fireflies 22 calls: 10 onboarding, 12 account reviews), mentions per theme, route and month, 129 text records, and an estimated cost; `--seed 43 --dry-run` prints the held-out plan (42 text records, data.md section 8.2).
- [ ] A sonnet subagent runs, after a probe, `uv run keelwater generate --seed 42 --max-usd 0.90` then `uv run keelwater generate --seed 43 --max-usd 0.30`. Seed 42 writes data/raw/** (data.md section 8.5 layout) and data/ground_truth.yaml (section 8.6 schema) and prints: gong 25 calls, intercom 60 files, fireflies 22 files, fullstory 40 sessions and about 1,200 events, hubspot 36 companies, shortcut 12 stories, notion 10 pages. Seed 43 writes data/holdout/raw/** and data/holdout/ground_truth.yaml. Total spend under USD 1.20.
- [ ] `uv run keelwater generate --seed 42 --force` and `--seed 43 --force`, run again offline from generator/cache, leave `git status --short` empty: both datasets are reproducible byte for byte. Without `--force`, generate refuses to overwrite.
- [ ] Every file under data/raw and data/holdout/raw validates against its contracts/sources schema (test).
- [ ] The verification of data.md section 8.2 passes for both seeds and is tested, plus: each real theme of seed 42 has at least 3 mentions dated September and 3 dated October (the stability replay needs both months); the loud-narrow probe is adversarial (below); the HubSpot mess and join traps of sections 4 and 6.3 are present; 10 seed-42 FullStory sessions run over 90 minutes with at least 80% idle time.
- [ ] Real-name check: no record contains a company or person name outside the spec files. A test plants an invented name that is not in the spec (for example "Brackenford Mutual") and the check flags it.
- [ ] Leak tests (data.md section 9 rule 5, extended): no module in signal_engine outside signal_engine/evals references data/ground_truth.yaml, data/holdout/ or generator/spec, or imports generator (signal_engine/cli.py is exempt: it registers `generate`); no theme title, fact phrase or synonym term of either seed appears under data/raw, data/holdout/raw, prompts/ or config/ (config/taxonomy.yaml included).
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` passes; counts posted in the PR.

## Scope

- generator/spec/accounts.yaml: data.md section 4, all 36 HubSpot records including the 2 stale duplicates (A06, A15), ARR in mixed formats in `keelwater_arr_gbp`, the `annualrevenue` trap, the null renewal for A22 and one lower-case tier.
- generator/spec/themes.yaml: data.md sections 6.1 and 6.2, with per-theme fact lists and synonym terms you write from the descriptions (mark invented values ASSUMED in comments), stances, product references, hard negatives, expected outcomes and the 10 one-off long-tail requests. Two review rulings, both already in data.md:
  - Account management has 12 account reviews (QBRs), so its 31 mentions fit at most 3 per record.
  - The loud-narrow probe (lt-welsh-templates) is adversarial: six mentions from one Strategic account renewing within 90 days of 03/11/2026, severity 4, across three routes (sales, support, account_management). Check with the formula of architecture section 4 that it scores below all six real themes, and say in the PR by how much.
- generator/spec/holdout/themes.yaml and noise.yaml for seed 43: three real themes and one noise theme that seed 42 does not contain, as specified in docs/data.md section 6.4, each real theme with at least 4 accounts across at least 2 routes, plus the usual noise mix. About 40% of seed 42's volume: Gong 10 calls, Intercom 24, Fireflies 8 (4 onboarding, 4 reviews), FullStory 16 sessions; HubSpot, Shortcut and Notion copied from seed 42. `--seed 43` writes only under data/holdout/.
- generator/spec/noise.yaml (data.md section 6.3, distractors included), people.yaml (Keelwater staff by team and customer contacts; every domain ends in `.example`) and glossary.yaml (the product feature names the prompt allows).
- config/teams.yaml written from people.yaml (Keelwater staff email to sales, support, onboarding or account_management).
- The seven steps of data.md section 8.2 and the per-record prompt of section 8.3 (generator/prompts/record.md). The prompt also forbids any real company, product or person name: use only the names given in the record brief. Model `mistralai/mistral-large-4-0` at temperature 0.8, up to 8 parallel calls, at most 2 regenerations per failing record; a seeded RNG drives every code-side choice.
- Real-name check, run in step 6 (verify): collect capitalised words and multi-word sequences that do not start a sentence; anything not in accounts.yaml, people.yaml, glossary.yaml or a short list of allowed common words (months, days, UK place names used in the spec) fails the record, which is regenerated; after 2 retries the run aborts and lists record id and token. `# shortcut: capitalisation heuristic, upgrade to an NER pass if a real export is ever generated from`.
- FullStory and HubSpot written by code only (section 8.2 steps 4 and 5).
- Shortcut: 12 stories including 4127 "Bulk upload documents to a claim", completed 06/10/2026, and the not-started spike "Document classifier confidence threshold". Notion: 10 pages including "Policyholder milestone notifications" (In progress, target Q1 2027) and "Reserve history audit export" (Planned).
- Commit generator/spec, generator/prompts, generator/cache, data/ and data/holdout/.

## Out of scope

- Any pipeline stage; public datasets; regeneration tooling beyond `--force`.
- Tuning anything on seed 43. Nobody reads generator/spec/holdout/ or data/holdout/ground_truth.yaml outside this issue and the holdout suite in #7.

## Skills

- ponytail; engineering:testing-strategy (verification, real-name and leak tests).

## Engine routing

- Machine: `laptop`, L1 orchestrator, worktree `.worktrees/issue-2`
- Model: `opus` orchestrator; build by `terra` (codex plugin); generation run and PR check by `sonnet` subagents
- Effort: `high` (opus), `high` (terra), `high` (sonnet)
- Parallel: `yes, with #1 for the spec and code-only steps; integrate after #1 merges; then beside #3 and #5`

```
Implement #2
```

- Do not send to any external model, codex included: `.env`, the values of OPENROUTER_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_API_KEY, the publish deny-list file.
- Live calls: a sonnet subagent (keys load from the main checkout's `.env`) runs `uv run keelwater probe --stages generate`, then the two generation runs; caps USD 0.90 (seed 42) and 0.30 (seed 43). The codex worker never runs live steps.
- Review: orchestrator's sonnet check only.

## Human steps

- #14 before the generation step; build and test the code-only steps first.

## Checks

- `uv run pytest -q`: post the pass/fail counts.
- Paste both dry-run outputs, both generation summaries (records, calls, regenerations, names flagged, spend), the probe's score margin, and the empty `git status --short` after the `--force` re-runs.

## Output

- Final issue comment as set out in the `reporting` section of AGENTS.md, titled "#2 Synthetic data: seed 42, held-out seed 43 and planted ground truth: Done".
- List every spec value you had to invent (ASSUMED), any record that needed regeneration, and any taxonomy description you reworded. Do not paste the held-out themes into the comment: name only their count.

## Teardown

- Delete generator/build/ and `.scratch/`; stop every process you started.
- Report free disk before and after (`df -h .` in Git Bash, or `Get-PSDrive C` in PowerShell).

items.title: Implement central redaction pipeline applied across all observable surfaces
items.body:
Part of #3

## Context
Architecture doc §9.4 (Redaction boundary) and ADR-016. Redaction is centralized specifically so each adapter/exporter doesn't reimplement it inconsistently. Every observable exit (logs, spans, metrics, audit, Explorer, serialized errors) passes through this one pipeline before data leaves the process.

## Interface
```ts
interface RedactionRule {
  readonly id: string;
  matches(field: RedactionContext): boolean;
  transform(value: unknown): unknown;   // typically returns '[REDACTED]' or a hash
}

interface RedactionPipeline {
  redact(value: unknown, context: RedactionContext): unknown;
  add(rule: RedactionRule): void;
}

interface RedactionContext {
  readonly surface: 'log' | 'span' | 'metric' | 'audit' | 'explorer' | 'error';
  readonly path: readonly string[];       // JSON path from root
  readonly operationId?: string;
}
```

## Built-in rules
Ship a default rule set covering the common cases:
- **Key-name allowlist-based** — `password`, `token`, `apiKey`, `authorization`, `secret`, `credential`, `ssn`, `cvv`, `pin`, etc.
- **Header-value patterns** — `Authorization: Bearer *` → `Authorization: [REDACTED]`.
- **Structured-value patterns** — credit-card-number-shaped, JWT-shaped strings.
- **PII surface-specific** — Explorer/log strip more aggressively than audit (audit needs some determinism for `inputDigest`).

Rules are ordered — first match wins. User rules are inserted after built-ins by default.

## Surfaces plugged into the pipeline
Per §9.4:
1. **Log emitter** — every `LogFields` object.
2. **Span attribute writer** — every OTel span attribute.
3. **Metric attribute writer** — labels checked against a stricter allowlist (label leakage is worse than log leakage).
4. **Audit projection** — full audit event just before sink.append.
5. **Explorer call history** — before serialization to the client.
6. **Serialized error path** — the OperationError-to-wire mapping.

## Enforcement
- Add a CI test that snapshots the outputs of each surface for a "known secret" fixture: input containing `token: 'sk_live_xyz'`. Each of the 6 surfaces' snapshot must contain `[REDACTED]` (or the configured form) and never `sk_live_xyz`.
- A negative test: adding a new surface without wiring it into redaction fails the snapshot check.

## Metrics
- `mcp_redaction_hits_total{rule, surface}` — helps operators see which rules are firing.

## Non-goals
- Structured-schema redaction (per-field flags) — deferred to Ecosystem overlays.
- Payload capture with customer-controlled projection — that's the commercial observability tier (§20.3.E), never open-source default.

## Tests
- Sixfold-surface snapshot for a known-secret fixture.
- Rule ordering: user rule runs after built-ins but before final serialization.
- Metric-attribute allowlist: attempting to add a redacted-then-labelled value → still stripped or refused.

## Acceptance
- Six surfaces flow through the pipeline.
- CI snapshot test guards against future surface additions bypassing redaction.
- Documented as the single point of truth for what leaves the process.

items.title: Implement EU Omnibus Directive (Price Reduction Transparency)
items.body:
## Summary

Implement support for the EU Omnibus Directive (EU 2019/2161), which requires displaying the lowest price from the previous 30 days when announcing a price reduction. This is mandatory for e-commerce in EU member states since May 28, 2022.

## Background

The Omnibus Directive amended the Price Indication Directive (PID) by adding Article 6a, which requires that any "price reduction announcement" must show the prior price, defined as the **lowest price applied by the trader during at least 30 days** before the reduction.

Non-compliance can result in fines up to **4% of annual turnover** or at least €2 million.

## Critical clarification: ECJ C-330/23 (Aldi Süd, 26 Sept 2024)

The Court of Justice of the EU ruled that **any announced reduction (percentage or promotional statement) must be determined on the basis of the prior price**, not merely accompanied by a separate disclaimer mentioning it.

Confirmed by:
- MiMIT FAQ no. 4 (Italy)
- AICEL guidelines (Italy)
- AGCM PS12820 sanctions (Tannico case)
- White & Case legal analysis

Practical consequence for our implementation: it is **not sufficient** to keep the original/higher price as the strikethrough and add a "lowest 30-day price was €Y" note next to it. The strikethrough itself must be the 30-day lowest, and any percentage badge must be computed from it. See [the discussion thread](https://github.com/MahoCommerce/maho/issues/453) for source references.

## Legal Requirements

### What IS covered (requires 30-day lowest price display)

| Type | Example |
|------|---------|
| Crossed-out prices | ~~€50~~ €35 |
| Percentage/amount discounts | "20% off", "Save €15" |
| General sale announcements | "Sale", "Black Friday" |
| Public coupon codes | Codes announced to the general public |

### What is NOT covered

| Type | Reasoning |
|------|-----------|
| Loyalty programs | Extended continuous periods (6mo/1yr), or point accumulation |
| Personal vouchers | Received after purchase, birthday discounts, truly personalized |
| Conditional/tied offers | "Buy 2 get 1 free", "30% off when buying 3" |
| Checkout-only discounts | Price shown only in cart when condition is met |
| Price comparisons | RRP, competitor prices |
| Cash-back offers | Third-party refund arrangements |

### Exceptions allowed by member states

- Goods liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly (perishables)
- Products on the market for less than 30 days (shorter period allowed)
- Progressive price reductions (reference can be price before first reduction)

## Maho Features Affected

| Feature | Omnibus Applies? | Notes |
|---------|------------------|-------|
| **Special Price** (product attribute) | **Yes** | Visible price reduction with dates |
| **Catalog Price Rules** | **Yes** | When displayed as crossed-out or % off |
| **Cart Price Rules** | **Depends** | Public codes yes, personal codes no |
| **Tier Prices** | **No** | Conditional on quantity purchased |
| **Group Prices** | **No** | Loyalty/membership pricing |
| **Maho_FeedManager** (Google, Bing, Facebook, Pinterest, Idealo, Trovaprezzi, GoogleLocalInventory, Openai, Custom) | **Yes** | Public reduction announcements rendered on external platforms |

## Product Type Handling

| Product Type | What to Track | Display Behavior |
|--------------|---------------|------------------|
| **Simple** | Product price | Strikethrough = 30-day low (or no strikethrough if current >= 30-day low) |
| **Virtual/Downloadable** | Product price | Same as Simple |
| **Configurable** | Each simple variant separately | Per-variant 30-day low used as strikethrough; updates with JS on variant change |
| **Grouped** | Each associated product separately | Per-child 30-day low used as strikethrough beside each product |
| **Bundle (Fixed)** | Minimum configuration price | Strikethrough = 30-day low of min config |
| **Bundle (Dynamic)** | Minimum configuration price | Strikethrough = 30-day low of min config |

## Proposed Implementation

### New Module: `Maho_Omnibus`

Separate module rather than core-patched. Core placement would require either rewriting `Mage_Catalog_Model_Product::getPrice()` (breaking cart math, indexer, and admin grids that share the same getter) or duplicating the same logic in two places. A clean module with a helper API keeps coupling to one block rewrite + one FeedManager placeholder + a small admin UI surface.

```
app/code/core/Maho/Omnibus/
├── Block/
│   └── Product/
│       └── Price.php                # Rewrite of Mage_Catalog_Block_Product_Price
├── Helper/
│   └── Data.php                     # Public API + isEnabled() check
├── Model/
│   ├── Observer.php                 # #[Observer] price tracking + #[CronJob] cleanup
│   ├── History.php                  # Price history model
│   └── Resource/
│       ├── History.php              # Resource model
│       └── History/
│           └── Collection.php
├── etc/
│   ├── config.xml                   # Block rewrite declaration
│   └── system.xml                   # catalog/omnibus/* config under Catalog section
└── sql/
    └── omnibus_setup/
        └── install-1.0.0.php        # Create price history table
```

Observers and cron jobs are registered via PHP attributes (`#[Maho\Config\Observer]`, `#[Maho\Config\CronJob]`) per current Maho conventions, not via `config.xml`.

### Helper API (the seam everything else calls)

```php
Mage::helper('omnibus')->isEnabled(int $storeId): bool
Mage::helper('omnibus')->getReferencePrice(Mage_Catalog_Model_Product $product, ?int $storeId = null): ?float
Mage::helper('omnibus')->shouldAnnounceReduction(Mage_Catalog_Model_Product $product, float $currentPrice, ?int $storeId = null): bool
```

- `getReferencePrice()` returns the 30-day low for the product/store, or `null` if no usable history (grace period, new product).
- `shouldAnnounceReduction()` returns `false` when `current_price >= 30day_low`, suppressing the strikethrough and any percentage badge entirely.

**Customer-group scoping**: Omnibus applies only to publicly-announced consumer reductions. Snapshots are captured against the guest / NOT_LOGGED_IN view of each store, and the block rewrite returns `null` (no Omnibus substitution, native strikethrough behaviour falls through) when the visitor is in a non-default customer group. This honours the directive's B2B and loyalty-program exemptions without forcing those catalogs to comply with a B2C rule.

### Display layer behaviour

Implemented as a rewrite of `Mage_Catalog_Block_Product_Price`:

1. The struck-through price becomes the 30-day lowest, not `regular_price` or the most recent `special_price`.
2. Any %-off badge or "Save €X" claim is computed as `(30day_low − current) / 30day_low`.
3. If `current_price >= 30day_low`, no reduction is announced at all (no strikethrough, no badge), even when `special_price` is set in admin. This is a deliberate behaviour change merchants need to be aware of.
4. New products under the grace period: no strikethrough rendered.

**Implementation note**: the block rewrite exposes a single `getOmnibusReferencePrice()` method returning the raw 30-day low (or `null` to suppress the strikethrough). The `catalog/product/price.phtml` template integration is two lines at line 53 — substituting the source of `$_convertedPrice`. All 24 downstream tax/Weee/percentage branches inherit the corrected value automatically because they derive from `$_regularPrice`, which derives from `$_convertedPrice`. No duplication of tax helper or Weee renderer logic.

### Tax and Weee handling

Snapshots store the raw `getFinalPrice()` at qty=1 — pre-tax, pre-Weee, pre-currency-conversion. At render time the value flows through the same `Mage_Tax_Helper_Data::getPrice()` + Weee renderer pipeline as the current price, guaranteeing strikethrough and current price are always in matching tax/Weee representation regardless of `tax/display/type`, `price_includes_tax`, cross-border-trade, FPT taxability, or display zone.

Trade-off accepted: a VAT rate change after a snapshot recomputes the historical displayed value through the new rate. This is consistent with how the rest of catalog display behaves and is a defensible reading of "lowest applied price in the last 30 days" (the merchant's offered base price, not pixel-identical historical rendering).

### Maho_FeedManager integration

Add a new template placeholder `{omnibus_lowest_price_30d}` exposed by `ProductProcessorTrait::_getProductValueForTemplate()`, resolving to the 30-day lowest price for the product in the feed's target store. Default feed templates remain unchanged, so existing installs see no behaviour change on upgrade.

Merchants who want Google Shopping / Idealo / Trovaprezzi to display Omnibus-compliant discount badges edit their adapter template and substitute `{price}` for `{omnibus_lowest_price_30d}`. Per-merchant, per-adapter opt-in.

Rationale for placeholder-only (vs. an automatic hook that rewrites `price` and `sale_price`): the feed is just data — the merchant owns the template, and platform-level enforcement (Google Merchant Center, Idealo policy) is a merchant compliance decision, not Maho's choice to force. The same opt-in philosophy as the per-store frontend toggle.

### Admin UI

Two surfaces, no general dashboard. No new columns on the global Products grid (already crowded) and no full-history snapshot dashboard (the audit trail is accessible per-product via the Prices tab and in bulk via CSV export).

**Product edit → Prices tab**:

- 90-day price history chart with 30-day rolling-low overlay
- "Currently announcing reduction" status banner at the top of the tab
- Compliance warning rendered next to `special_price` when the planned change wouldn't actually trigger a strikethrough (current ≥ 30-day low) — catches the merchant misconception in admin before it ships to storefront

**Catalog → Omnibus Compliance** (new admin page):

- Filtered grid: products currently announcing a reduction, one row per product (not per snapshot)
- Columns: SKU, name, current price, 30-day low, computed %, anti-pattern flag (price raised in the 7 days before current reduction started), days remaining in reference window
- CSV export action for regulator-facing audit trail
- Click row → product edit, deep-linked to Prices tab + history anchor (`?active_tab=prices#omnibus_history`)
- Reverse link from the Prices-tab chart back to the Compliance page when the product is in the filtered set

The Compliance page is bounded by definition (only products with active reductions), so even on a 50k-product catalog the grid stays small.

### Database Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE omnibus_price_history (
    history_id INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    store_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    price DECIMAL(20,6) NOT NULL,
    recorded_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
    price_type ENUM('regular', 'special', 'catalog_rule', 'bundle_min') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'regular',

    INDEX idx_product_store (product_id, store_id),
    INDEX idx_recorded_at (recorded_at),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES catalog_product_entity(entity_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES core_store(store_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

### Configuration (System > Configuration > Catalog > Omnibus)

| Path | Scope | Default | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------------|
| `catalog/omnibus/enabled` | **store** | `0` | Master toggle, per-store so a single install can serve EU + non-EU stores from one backend |
| `catalog/omnibus/reference_period_days` | store | `30` | Configurable for different member state derogations |
| `catalog/omnibus/include_catalog_rules` | store | `1` | Track catalog price rule discounts |
| `catalog/omnibus/new_product_grace_days` | store | `30` | Days before a product has enough history to show a reference |
| `catalog/omnibus/cleanup_history_after_days` | store | `90` | Prune old records via cron |

**Default off**, with an admin notice on the Catalog config page when the store's default country resolves to an EU member state and the flag is off, nudging merchants toward enabling it without forcing.

History recording is also gated by the toggle: when disabled, observers skip entirely (no schema bloat or write cost on installs that won't use it). Tooltip documents the 30-day warmup period that begins when the flag is first enabled.

### Price tracking via observers

PHP attribute observers fire on:
- `catalog_product_save_after` (captures price, special_price changes)
- `catalogrule_after_apply` (captures catalog price rule activations)
- `catalog_product_import_bunch_save_after` (captures import-driven changes)

### Cleanup cron

`#[CronJob('omnibus_cleanup', schedule: '0 3 * * *')]` prunes records older than `cleanup_history_after_days`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create module structure (`Maho_Omnibus`) with per-store opt-in config
- [ ] Create database schema and install script
- [ ] Implement price history model and resource model
- [ ] Implement helper API: `isEnabled()`, `getReferencePrice()`, `shouldAnnounceReduction()`
- [ ] Create observer for `catalog_product_save_after` (via `#[Observer]` attribute)
- [ ] Create observer for `catalogrule_after_apply`
- [ ] Create observer for product import event
- [ ] Implement lowest-price calculation logic with grace period for new products
- [ ] Handle configurable products (track simple variants)
- [ ] Handle grouped products (track each associated product)
- [ ] Handle bundle products (fixed + dynamic, track minimum configuration)
- [ ] **Rewrite `Mage_Catalog_Block_Product_Price` to substitute strikethrough with 30-day low and compute percentage from it**
- [ ] **Suppress strikethrough/badge entirely when `current >= 30day_low`**
- [ ] Integrate with product page, category listings, search results, related/upsell/cross-sell, wishlist, compare, layered nav AJAX
- [ ] **Add `{omnibus_lowest_price_30d}` placeholder to `Maho_FeedManager/Model/Generator/ProductProcessorTrait.php` (opt-in via template edit, no default behaviour change)**
- [ ] Create cron job for history cleanup (via `#[CronJob]` attribute)
- [ ] **Admin notice on Catalog config page when EU country detected and Omnibus flag is off**
- [ ] **Product edit → Prices tab: 90-day history chart with 30-day rolling-low overlay**
- [ ] **Product edit → Prices tab: reduction status banner + admin-time compliance warning next to `special_price`**
- [ ] **Catalog → Omnibus Compliance admin page: filtered grid of products currently announcing reductions, with anti-pattern flag and CSV export**
- [ ] **Deep-link from Compliance page row to Prices tab (`?active_tab=prices#omnibus_history`)**
- [ ] Write tests across all scenarios (Pest)
- [ ] Documentation

## Edge Cases to Handle

1. **Product just created**: no history yet, grace period applies, no strikethrough rendered.
2. **Price never reduced (current >= 30-day low)**: no reduction announced at all, even if `special_price` is set.
3. **Multiple price changes same day**: each captured (event-based).
4. **Catalog rules with date ranges**: captured when rules activate/deactivate.
5. **Currency switching**: prices stored in base currency, converted for display.
6. **Logged-in customers with group-specific prices**: block rewrite returns `null` for non-default groups (B2B / loyalty exemption), native strikethrough behaviour falls through. Snapshots are NOT_LOGGED_IN scoped.
7. **Configurable product variant selected via JS**: dynamically updates strikethrough to that variant's 30-day low.
8. **Bundle minimum price changes**: recalculated when selections change.
9. **Multi-store EU + non-EU install**: per-store flag isolates behaviour per view.
10. **Feed regeneration after history accumulates**: feeds pick up corrected references on next scheduled generation.

## Cost Estimate

Updated to account for the FeedManager simplification (placeholder vs. automatic hook), the admin UI expansion (Prices-tab integration + Catalog → Omnibus Compliance page), and the schema simplification (customer_group_id column dropped):

| Scenario | Hours | Cost (€30/h) |
|----------|-------|--------------|
| Optimistic | 105h | €3,150 |
| **Realistic** | **145h** | **€4,350** |
| Conservative | 162h | €4,860 |

Net change vs. previous estimate (€4,290):

- FeedManager simplification (single placeholder, no automatic rewriting across nine adapters): **−6 to −8h**
- Admin UI expansion (Prices-tab chart + status banner + special_price compliance warning + Compliance admin page + CSV export + deep-link): **+10 to +12h** above the original "optional admin grid" baseline
- Schema simplification (drop `customer_group_id`, simpler index, no per-group query logic): **−1 to −2h**
- Tax/Weee handling reuses the existing `Mage_Tax_Helper_Data::getPrice()` + Weee renderer pipeline via raw-value snapshots: **+0h** (no new pipeline)

Net: roughly +2 to +4 hours, comfortably absorbed by the previous contingency.

## References

- [EU Directive 2019/2161 (Omnibus)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/2161/oj)
- [European Commission Guidance (PDF)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52021XC1229(06))
- [ECJ C-330/23 (Aldi Süd, 26 Sept 2024) summary](https://lawyersweek.net/24305/cjeu-c-330-23-aldi-sud-a-price-reduction-announced-in-an-advertisement-must-be-calculated-on-the-basis-of-the-lowest-price-in-the-last-30-days.html)
- [White & Case alert on C-330/23](https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/new-ecj-judgement-price-indication-directive-implications-online-retailers-and)
- [MiMIT FAQ (Italian Ministry of Enterprises)](https://www.mimit.gov.it/it/assistenza/domande-frequenti/annunci-di-riduzione-di-prezzo-domande-frequenti-faq)
- [AICEL Omnibus guide](https://www.aicel.org/come-fare-per/omnibus-annunci-di-riduzione-di-prezzo.html)
- [AGCM PS12820 Tannico decision](https://www.agcm.it/dotcmsdoc/allegati-news/PS12820_scorr.+sanz._omi..pdf)
- [Bird & Bird transparency analysis](https://www.twobirds.com/en/insights/2025/global/transparency-of-price-reductions-a-closer-look-at-the-legal-framework-in-the-eu)
- [Talon.One EU price reduction requirements](https://www.talon.one/blog/eu-requirements-for-advertising-with-price-reductions)
