Current state (mapped):
- The board order card (`app/httpapi_templates.py:762-779`) shows quantity inline in the wording text (`q.quantity + unit`), NOT editable; price is nowhere — no price field exists in `order_questions` (`teach.py:88-90` `_COLS`), in `_decision_dict` (`pipeline.py:117-120`), or in `order_items` (`worker.py:147-154`).
- Answering an item question (`POST /api/orders/question/<qid>/answer`, `httpapi_orders_questions.py:392-456`) writes item_memory and releases the held order → the EDI ships with the ORIGINAL extracted quantities; the human cannot correct a misread qty/price before it ships.

Feature:
1. Extraction/storage: capture unit price per order line where present in the source mail (extract prompt + `order_items`/question payload/schema migration via `migrate.py` engine), so the board has it to display.
2. Board UI: per product line show quantity and price on the right as editable fields prefilled with extracted values; OK confirms the line set (per-order confirm).
3. Answer flow: the confirmed/corrected values are what ships — the release path uses the human-confirmed quantities (and price, IF the ORION ORDER_ EDI format carries a price field — investigate; if the wire format has no price, price stays a verification display + stored correction, honestly labeled).
4. Scope of v1: orders that ALREADY land on the board (held orders with open questions, review orders with extracted lines). Mails short-circuited by a taught `mail_rules` "manual" rule (no extraction runs — `pipeline.py:170-176`) are a separate decision pending with the owner (asked 2026-08-21); do not change their behavior until answered.

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

The pipeline runs end to end for the first time. A stored Shipment Request gets read by the model, and code assigns a Decision — but only the coarsest one. Nothing accepts itself yet.

After intake responds, a background task makes one structured-output call. The same call classifies and extracts: `is_shipment_request`, `is_hazardous`, both Locations, the pickup date phrase as written, goods description, `{value, unit}` weight, pieces, and `unsure_fields`. Per ADR-0001 the model reports what it saw; no conversions, no calendar maths. The customer's text goes into the prompt inside a marked block, labelled as data.

The provider sits behind an interface with a fake implementation, so tests and CI need no API key.

Decisions at this stage: `is_shipment_request` false → **rejected**, and nothing else is evaluated. Extraction that fails after three retries with exponential backoff → **needs_review** with an `extraction_failed` Blocking Reason and no fields, which is exactly today's manual process. Everything else → **needs_review**.

`evals/decisions` and the case file format land here, running against the fake in CI on every push (ADR-0005), so the suite grows with the rules rather than being retrofitted. Write the adversarial cases first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extraction runs in a background task after intake responds; the caller never waits for it
- [ ] One structured-output call per request, using a Pydantic schema — no free-text parsing
- [ ] The customer's message sits inside a marked, labelled data block in the prompt
- [ ] The provider is behind an interface with a fake implementation; no test or CI run needs an API key
- [ ] The Extraction is stored immutably, alongside `model`, `prompt_version`, tokens in and out, and latency
- [ ] Each call logs model, tokens in and out, latency, and a trace id
- [ ] A non-freight message becomes `rejected` and is still stored
- [ ] Extraction failure retries three times with exponential backoff, then becomes `needs_review` with `extraction_failed` and no fields
- [ ] Schema-invalid model output follows the same path as any other failure
- [ ] Everything else becomes `needs_review`; nothing can be accepted automatically yet
- [ ] The Decision is assigned in `core`; the Extraction can never set it
- [ ] `evals/decisions` runs in CI against the fake, keyed by case name, raising on an unknown key
- [ ] The eval suite scores field accuracy and decision accuracy separately
- [ ] `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, and `uv run mypy --strict app/core` all pass

## Blocked by

- #3

items.title: Multi-environment deploy: per-env UC catalogs + multi-profile promotion (deploy-code MLOps)
items.body:
Highest-leverage gap toward fitting the canonical Databricks **"deploy code"** MLOps reference architecture (dev → staging → prod workspaces, code promoted via Git branches). Today apx-agent deploys to a single workspace per `--profile` with catalog/schema baked at scaffold time, so a customer's existing multi-workspace pipeline can't drive an apx agent through environments without hand-wiring.

### What's missing today
- **Per-environment UC catalogs** — catalog/schema are baked once at scaffold (`DataAgent("{catalog}","{schema}")`, e.g. `cli.py:1043`). No `dev_catalog`/`staging`/`prod_catalog` parameterization; the generated DAB exposes no catalog variable per target (`cli.py:1377`).
- **Multi-profile / multi-workspace promotion** — `--target` is a deploy *kind* (`model-serving`/`apps`), not an environment. One `--profile` = one workspace; the DAB's dev/prod modes resolve to the same workspace, with no `staging` and no `workspace.host` per target (`cli.py:1495`). `_fleet.py` is bulk ops over one profile, so it doesn't help here.

### Scope
- [ ] Parameterize UC catalog/schema by environment so the same agent def deploys against dev/staging/prod catalogs without re-scaffolding.
- [ ] Bind a deploy target to a workspace (per-env `--profile` / `workspace.host`) so promotion across dev→staging→prod is a first-class action, not a manual re-run.
- [ ] Wire it through both deploy paths (model-serving via `databricks.agents.deploy`; Apps via DAB targets).
- [ ] Keep the existing single-workspace default working (no behavior change when no envs are declared).

### Already in place (build on, don't duplicate)
- Validation gate: `apx-agent eval` (Mosaic AI scorers) + `apx-agent label` judge-alignment.
- Pre-cutover vetting: endpoint canary (`_canary.py`) + LLM hot-swap (`_hot_swap.py`).
- UC registration + single `@prod` alias (`_apps_registry.py:58`).

Context: assessed against the customer "deploy code" CI/CD diagram — apx emits the right primitives (UC pyfunc, DAB, `databricks.agents.deploy`) but provides no multi-workspace orchestration. This issue closes the orchestration gap on the apx side.

  - [x] Task 10: Extended `CustomerMaster` schema (this app's customer entity per the brief contact-is-NC-entity rule — no separate Counterparty schema invented) with VAT-ID verification fields per REQ-ICP-001, REQ-ICP-009: `vatId` (canonical EU form), `vatIdValidatedAt`, `vatIdValidUntil`, `vatIdValidationStatus` (unchecked/valid/invalid/vies_outage).   - [x] Task 11: Declare `x-openregister-lifecycle` on `IcpOpgaaf` per REQ-ICP-004, REQ-ICP-005 with states: `draft` → `finalized` (gate: reconciliation check against rubriek 3b per REQ-ICP-004, SBR schema validation per REQ-ICP-005) → `submitted` (approval workflow per ADR-022) → `accepted` / `rejected` / `corrected` (post-Belastingdienst states).
  - [x] Task 12: VIES validation implemented in `lib/Service/ViesService.php` — calls the EU VIES REST proxy via `IClientService`, canonicalises the VAT-ID, persists an immutable `ViesValidation` record (with `requestId` audit proof), and on a transient outage reuses a recent (< 30 days) valid record and flags `outage: true` for the daily retry job (REQ-ICP-001, REQ-ICP-009). (Spec corrected: implemented against the owned `ViesValidation` schema rather than the not-yet-existent `Invoice.icpContext`; re-attaches as a declarative calculation when AR-core declares Invoice.)

  - [x] Task 15: Implement ICP ledger aggregation as `x-openregister-aggregations` query per REQ-ICP-003 — GROUP BY `(buyerVatId, supplyType)`, SUM amounts (with sign preservation for credit notes), sort by buyerVatId.
  - [x] Task 16: Implement reconciliation gate on `IcpOpgaaf.finalize()` per REQ-ICP-004 — read period's submitted/draft BTW-aangifte, compare `IcpOpgaaf.total` against `BtwAangifte.rubriek3b`, allow EUR 1 tolerance, block with drill-down if diverge.
  - [x] Task 17: Implement triangulation handling per REQ-ICP-006 — on `Invoice.icpContext.supplyType: T`, validate C-party VAT-ID (not A-party) against VIES, aggregate separately on `(buyerVatId, T)` line (never merged with L or S).
  - [x] Task 18: AR invoice ICP overlay rendering shipped in `lib/Service/ArInvoiceIcpPdfRenderer.php` + `IcpController::renderInvoicePdf()` (exposed at `GET /api/icp/invoice-pdf`). On `ARInvoice.icpContext.treatAsIcp: true` the document includes the buyer VAT-ID (C-party for triangulation supplies per REQ-ICP-006), the seller NL VAT-ID, the "VAT reverse-charged" notice (Dutch translation: "BTW verlegd" via the i18n layer), and the supply-type label (Goods / Services / Triangulation). Rendering loudly fails with HTTP 422 + `icp.invoice.vatid.missing` when the buyer VAT-ID is absent (REQ-ICP-007). Pure unit-tested (`tests/Unit/Service/ArInvoiceIcpPdfRendererTest.php`). The HTML output is the canonical body; downstream PDF binarisation (mPDF / wkhtmltopdf / docudesk render pipeline) wraps it identically to the existing `InvoicePdfGenerator` pattern.
  - [x] Task 19: Correction workflow implemented in `IcpService::createCorrection()` — materialises a new `IcpOpgaaf` with `type: correction`, `correctsPeriod`, `correctionReason` and the aggregated corrective lines (positive/negative), re-attaching the original contemporaneous `ViesValidation` evidence by buyer VAT-ID (no VIES re-query, REQ-ICP-008) via `ViesService::findRecentValid()`. Starts in `draft` so the reconciliation gate still applies. Exposed as `POST /api/icp/correction`. Digipoort delivery of the correction is the openconnector integration (deferred — live instance).
  - [x] Task 20: VIES outage retry scheduling implemented in `lib/BackgroundJob/ViesOutageRetryJob.php` (TimedJob, 24h interval) + `IcpService::pendingOutages()` — distinguishes `valid: false` (definitive) from `outage: true` (transient), re-validates pending outages daily via `ViesService::validate()`, and escalates to the bookkeeper via the notification manager once an outage has persisted beyond 14 days (REQ-ICP-009, subject `icp.vies.outage_escalated`).
  - [x] Task 21: Audit-trail export implemented in `IcpService::exportForInspection()` — builds a `ZipArchive` bundle containing the archived XBRL payload (`opgaaf.xbrl`), the Belastingdienst `kenmerk.txt`, the `supplies.csv` of all supplies with their VIES request IDs (via `IcpCalculator::buildSuppliesCsv`), and a `manifest.txt` (REQ-ICP-010). Exposed as `GET /api/icp/audit-export` (the server temp path is stripped from the response — no path leak). Source-invoice PDF attachment (docudesk/OR file surface) is the deferred live-instance step.
  - [x] Task 22: Add 3 chart-of-accounts entries per proposal and design: `8190 Omzet ICP goederen` (zero-rated), `8195 Omzet ICP diensten` (zero-rated), `8196 Omzet ICP driehoekstransacties` (zero-rated), per RGS pattern; routing helper: supplyType L → 8190, S → 8195, T → 8196.
  - [x] Task 23: Add 3 manifest navigation entries per REQ-ICP-003, REQ-ICP-010: `ICP Supplies` (ledger view, lists all supplies aggregated by period/buyer), `ICP Filings` (list of submitted opgaven with status), `ICP Audit Trail` (inspection bundle export + compliance log) — plus their `type: index` and `type: detail` pages.
  - [x] Task 24: Update `openspec/architecture/adr-000-data-model.md` with `ViesValidation`, `IcpSupply`, `IcpOpgaaf`, `PeriodicitySwitch` entries, `Invoice.icpContext` extension, `Counterparty.vatId*` extension fields, reconciling against any existing `Vat*` / `Filing` data-model entries.
  - [x] Task 25: Create integration test fixtures (PHPUnit) for: VIES validation success/failure/outage scenarios, periodicity threshold detection and switch-back, ICP aggregation with credit notes, reconciliation mismatch detection, triangulation line separation, SBR XBRL schema validation, correction filing with evidence preservation, audit-trail ZIP export.
  - [x] Task 26: Playwright manifest-shell smoke shipped in `tests/e2e/icp-opgaaf.spec.ts` — confirms the ICP-opgaaf SPA route resolves inside the shillinq app namespace. Full end-to-end ICP flows (VIES round-trip, ledger drill-down, Digipoort submission, audit ZIP export) are documented as `@e2e exclude` in the spec module-doc and remain deferred: they require a live OpenRegister instance with openconnector VIES + Digipoort integrations seeded (out of this app's scope per the fragment `_meta`).

## Design
See [design.md](https://github.com/ConductionNL/shillinq/blob/development/openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-14-bookkeeping-icp-opgaaf/design.md) for technical design details.

Platform PRD §15.1 describes what to track and what to model but not how data is emitted. Phase 1 cost-telemetry requirement risks being "done" with empty tables. Without emission spec, the §17.1 ≤40%-COGS/MRR kill criterion is unobservable.

items.title: [sql] Reorganize sql/ into engine-symmetric layout with core/contract/customer layering + drift detection
items.body:
**Labels:** `sql`, `schema-migrator`, `tech-debt`, `oracle`, `postgres`

## Context

`sql/` mixed multiple organizing principles:

- Oracle split files lived under `sql/oracle/`, grouped by object type.
- Postgres split files lived loose at the top level of `sql/`, not under `sql/postgres/`.
- `sql/oracle.sql` and `sql/postgres.source.sql` were hand-maintained aggregate baselines that could drift from split files.
- `sql/postgres.sql` encoded apply order as a `psql`-specific `\ir` shim.
- Customer-specific changes were tracked by comment markers rather than by structure.

## Problem

1. No single source of truth per engine; split files and aggregate baselines could drift silently.
2. No dependency-order manifest that is tool-agnostic.
3. No structural separation between core schema, stable customer-facing contracts, and customer overlays.
4. No reliable way to detect customized objects independent of comments.
5. No CI-backed ephemeral database harness or object-level SQL tests.

## Goals

- [x] Symmetric, predictable directory layout for both engines.
- [x] Single source of truth per engine: split files are canonical; aggregate baselines are generated artifacts.
- [x] Engine-agnostic, explicit apply-order manifest replacing the `\ir` shim.
- [x] Three-tier layering: `core/` -> `contracts/` -> `customers/<name>/`.
- [ ] Deterministic, hash-based drift detection to identify customized objects independent of comments.
- [ ] Queryable registry of customization status per object per customer.
- [ ] CI-driven testing: ephemeral DBs, schema-diff snapshot tests, object-level unit tests, per-customer regression matrix, idempotency/rollback checks.

## Implementation Update (2026-07-04)

Completed in `schema-migrator`:

- Added symmetric engine roots: `sql/postgres/` and `sql/oracle/`.
- Moved split SQL into numbered `core/` object-type directories for both engines.
- Added `contracts/` and `customers/fixture/` layers for both engines.
- Added `manifest.yaml` per engine/layer.
- Added manifest-aware discovery with legacy folder-order fallback.
- Added `--customer <name>` so customer overlays are opt-in.
- Added `generate-baseline`, which writes `_generated_baseline.sql` from manifest order.
- Ignored generated baselines via `.gitignore` so they are never hand-edited source.
- Removed the checked-in aggregate/shim source files from the SQL tree.

Remaining work is drift detection, the object customization registry, and CI database harness coverage.

## Directory Structure

```text
sql/
  postgres/
    core/
      00_extensions/
      01_schemas/
      02_types/
      03_tables/
      04_indexes/
      05_functions/
      06_views/
      07_materialized_views/
      08_triggers/
      09_cron/
      10_seed_data/
      manifest.yaml
    contracts/
      functions/
      views/
      CONTRACT.md
      manifest.yaml
    customers/
      <customer>/
        extensions/
        overrides/
        manifest.yaml
  oracle/
    core/
      00_session/
      01_extensions_n-a/
      02_types/
      03_tables/
      04_indexes/
      05_functions/
      06_packages/
      07_contexts/
      08_triggers/
      09_views/
      10_scheduler/
      11_security/
      12_ilm_policies/
      13_seed_data/
      manifest.yaml
    contracts/
      functions/
      views/
      CONTRACT.md
      manifest.yaml
    customers/
      <customer>/
        extensions/
        overrides/
        manifest.yaml
  teardown/
    oracle_nuclear_drop.sql
  registry/
```

## Manifest Format

```yaml
engine: postgres
layer: core
apply_order:
  - 00_extensions/001_extensions.sql
  - 01_schemas/001_coordinator.sql
  - 03_tables/001_sync_cursors.sql
```

Rules:

- `core/manifest.yaml` applies first.
- `contracts/manifest.yaml` applies second.
- `customers/<name>/manifest.yaml` applies only when `--customer <name>` is provided.
- Split SQL files are the source of truth.
- `_generated_baseline.sql` is generated by `generate-baseline` and ignored.

## Drift Detection Design (Remaining)

1. Canonical DDL for every core/contract object is the git-tracked split file.
2. A scheduled job pulls live DDL from each customer environment:
   - Oracle: `DBMS_METADATA.GET_DDL(object_type, object_name, owner)`.
   - Postgres: `pg_get_viewdef()`, `pg_get_functiondef()`, or object-scoped `pg_dump --schema-only`.
3. Normalize both definitions and hash with SHA-256.
4. Populate a registry table.

Example registry shape:

| object_name | object_type | owner_schema | core_hash | live_hash | status | last_checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v_device_inventory | VIEW | ACME_CUSTOM | a1f3... | a1f3... | in_sync | 2026-07-04 |
| v_wireless_threats | VIEW | ACME_CUSTOM | 9c02... | 7be1... | drifted | 2026-07-04 |

Structural attribution remains a second signal: customer objects should live under customer-specific schemas/owners.

## Testing Strategy (Remaining)

- [ ] Ephemeral DB per PR using Testcontainers or docker-compose.
- [ ] Schema-diff snapshot tests using `pg_dump --schema-only` and Oracle metadata dumps.
- [ ] Object-level unit tests with pgTAP and utPLSQL.
- [ ] Per-customer regression matrix before core releases.
- [ ] Idempotency test: apply twice.
- [ ] Rollback test: apply, rollback, re-apply.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `sql/oracle/` and `sql/postgres/` are symmetric trees.
- [x] No hand-maintained aggregate baseline files remain as source; baselines are generated artifacts.
- [x] `manifest.yaml` exists per engine/layer and is the source of apply order.
- [x] A fixture customer overlay demonstrates the `core -> contracts -> customers` chain.
- [ ] Drift detection job runs against a fixture customer DB and reports intentionally injected drift.
- [ ] CI pipeline applies the full manifest in an ephemeral DB and fails on schema-diff mismatch.
- [ ] Registry table schema is documented and queryable via `sql/registry/drift_report.sql`.

## Commands

```bash
# List Postgres core + contracts
sbt "run --db-kind postgres --sql-dir ./sql/postgres list"

# Include fixture customer overlay
sbt "run --db-kind postgres --sql-dir ./sql/postgres --customer fixture list"

# Validate without a live database
sbt "run --db-kind postgres --sql-dir ./sql/postgres validate"
sbt "run --db-kind oracle --sql-dir ./sql/oracle validate"

# Generate ignored aggregate artifacts
sbt "run --db-kind postgres --sql-dir ./sql/postgres generate-baseline"
sbt "run --db-kind oracle --sql-dir ./sql/oracle generate-baseline"
```

## Non-goals

- Full declarative/diff-based migration engine.
- Rewriting existing object DDL/logic.
- Automatically resolving detected drift.

## Open Questions

- Which engine's drift job should be built first: Oracle metadata or Postgres catalog extraction?
- Should the customization registry live entirely in `schema-migrator`, or should project-specific tables remain in consuming services?
- What is the first real customer overlay to promote from fixture to production coverage?

items.title: App: Payment processor integration (Stripe / PayPal / GoCardless pluggable)
items.body:
## What this app does

Pluggable payment processor framework supporting Stripe, PayPal, GoCardless (UK direct debit), and other providers. Used by the Giving app (#266) for card/recurring contributions and by the Projects app (#267) for pledge fulfillment.

**Industries served:** any org needing to accept payments — churches, nonprofits, professional associations (subscription dues), event organisers, schools (fees), small businesses.

**Specific church use case:** member sets up a £100/month standing-order-equivalent via GoCardless from their UK bank. Tithes are auto-collected; the giving log auto-populates.

## App pattern (per #255)

- **Slug:** `payments`
- **Route:** `/payments` (admin) + integration endpoints
- **Setting:** `payments.enabled` (default `0`)
- **Industry tags:** `church`, `nonprofit`, `events`, `school`, `small-business`, `membership-org`

## Architecture

`Portal\Core\PaymentProcessor` abstract class + per-provider implementations:
- `PaymentProcessorStripe`
- `PaymentProcessorPayPal`
- `PaymentProcessorGoCardless`
- (future) `PaymentProcessorSquare`, `PaymentProcessorStandingOrder` (manual reconciliation)

Each implements: `createCharge()`, `createRecurring()`, `cancelRecurring()`, `webhookVerify()`, `webhookHandle()`.

## Schema

- `tblPaymentMethod` — provider tokenised method per user (Stripe customer ID, PayPal billing agreement ID, GoCardless mandate ID)
- `tblPayment` — paymentID, userID, providerRef, amountPence, currency, status (pending/succeeded/failed/refunded), purpose (giving-entry / pledge / membership / other), purposeRef, occurredAt
- `tblWebhookEvent` — append-only log of incoming webhooks for replay debugging

## Pages

- `/payments` (admin) — provider configuration, fee structure, reconciliation reports
- `/account/payment-methods` — member manages their saved payment methods
- `/account/recurring` — member sees + cancels recurring payments
- `/api/payments/webhook/{provider}` — provider webhook endpoint

## Features

- PCI-DSS posture: no raw card data ever touches the portal. All payments via Stripe Elements / PayPal SDK / GoCardless Pro UI hosted on provider domain.
- Webhook signature verification per provider's spec.
- Idempotency keys to prevent duplicate charges.
- Test mode toggle (`payments.test_mode`) for sandbox/live switch.
- Fee transparency: each payment row stores `feeAmountPence` so reports show net vs gross.
- Refund flow.
- Failed-payment retry logic (provider-dependent).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PaymentProcessor` abstract + Stripe implementation (most-used).
- [ ] Webhook endpoint with signature verification.
- [ ] Test mode switch.
- [ ] Refund support.
- [ ] Integration with Giving (#266) + Projects (#267).
- [ ] PayPal + GoCardless as separate follow-up PRs.
- [ ] Registered in AppRegistry.

## Effort

XL (~1500-2500 LOC for Stripe; another L each for PayPal + GoCardless).

## Labels

- type: feature
- priority: medium
- scope: core

## Source
ADR 0011 (PR #918) §7 — routing_rules placeholder explicitly rejected at v1 ("a placeholder for a grammar that has not been designed is a TODO with extra steps"). When persona #2 ships, the grammar is forced by real requirements; design it then, against real input.

## What

Design the routing-rules grammar in `customer.yaml.routing_rules` (or whichever field name lands). The engine reads the rules and decides which persona handles a given inbound (email, calendar event, etc.). Each rule matches on sender / recipient / subject / channel / matter and binds to a persona_slug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Grammar designed (committed as ADR addendum or as a section in `customer-yaml-schema.md`):
  - [ ] Match criteria: sender address pattern, recipient address pattern, subject regex, matter_ref pattern, channel
  - [ ] Action: route to persona_slug, or "no match → default persona"
  - [ ] Precedence: ordered list, first match wins
  - [ ] Default persona declared at top of routing_rules (or inferred from `personas[0]`)
- [ ] Engine reads rules from customer.yaml at boot and on config reload
- [ ] Inbound email pipeline (post-AgentMail receipt) consults engine, hands the message to the matched persona's Hermes process via IPC
- [ ] Test fixtures cover: exact sender match, regex match, fall-through to default, no-default error case, archived-persona target (treated as no-match), conflicting rules
- [ ] Validator (in customer.yaml validator) catches: undefined persona_slug in rule, archived persona as target, circular default reference

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: customer.yaml schema spec update (#790)
- Blocked by: per-Machine supervisor (#925) — engine routes between processes the supervisor manages

items.title: [Security] §1 — Introduce the organization (org_id) layer as the real tenant boundary
items.body:
**Part of #87 · Plan §1 · `priority: critical` · foundation (load-bearing)**

## Status (verified @ `45c28ba`)
**Not started.** Workspace is currently the de-facto top-level tenant; there is **no `organization`/`org_id` layer above it.** Flyway `V1`–`V14` are all workspace-scoped; `TenantContext` carries only `workspaceId/userId/role`; no `Organization` bean exists; RBAC tables (`V13`) are FK'd to `workspace(id)`, not an org.

## What
Introduce an `organization` entity **above** workspaces. The org is the customer — the billing, contract, and breach boundary. Workspaces become sub-partitions inside an org (`workspace.org_id`).

## Why
The org boundary is the one that matters for isolation, billing, and the entrustee/DPA relationship, and it's the single most important structural piece still missing. A cross-org leak is a breach (must be impossible); a cross-workspace leak within an org is an internal-permissions matter (RBAC). Retrofitting org later is asymmetrically expensive — and §6 (CMK/key custody), §7 (silos), and §11 (AI/BYOP) all assume a clean org boundary exists.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add an `organization` table (the billing/contract/breach boundary = the customer).
- [ ] Add `org_id` to `workspace` and to every tenant-owned entity not reachable purely through a workspace FK; backfill existing rows to a single default org via a **forward-only** Flyway migration (`V15+`), non-destructive / expand-contract (§9).
- [ ] Make `org_id` the primary scoping key everywhere; treat `workspace_id` as the secondary internal partition. Update uniqueness anchors and composite FKs (currently `(workspace_id, id)`).
- [ ] Extend `TenantContext` to carry `orgId`; resolve + re-validate org membership per request in `TenantResolutionInterceptor` (fail-closed).
- [ ] Extend the `TenantScopeInterceptor` (commit `12a4523`) to require a resolved **org** context, not just workspace.
- [ ] Bind workspace RBAC to org context: a role is "admin within org X," never a global admin (`V13 workspace_role` has no org dimension today).
- [ ] Add cross-org isolation tests (org A cannot read/write org B) for every entity, including future AI/export read paths.
- [ ] Validate the org→workspace partitioning axis against a **named customer need** before semantics are locked (per §1: "Sales dept / Engineering dept" is an unusual CRM cut).

## Relationship to existing issues
Distinct from #61 (workspace-level multitenancy, largely landed) and #89 (read-scoping + interceptor, workspace-scoped). This is the layer above both. Gates #92 (§6), the deployment issues (§7–§9), and all AI work (#94/§11).

items.title: EOM lead funnel + operational CRM: current-state audit & gaps (lead capture, auto-reply, tenant separation, customer backfill)
items.body:
## Goal

Give Effingham Office Maids (EOM) a **clean, EOM-only operational CRM in Postgres** that captures new leads in real time, sends an instant "thank you / what to expect" acknowledgement on estimate-request submission, and manages leads, issues/complaints, customer scheduling, and per-visit pricing. This issue is the **current-state audit** (code as source of truth, not docs) and the **gap list**. No code has been changed yet.

Repo of record: `canfieldjuan/atlas` (backend CRM/email/tenant). The estimate form lives in `canfieldjuan/effingham_office_maids_website`.

---

## Funnel today (verified)

```
Google Ad -> effinghamofficemaids.com/contact
  form action -> https://api.web3forms.com/submit   (Web3Forms, 3rd-party form->email)
  -> emails the submission to the business inbox
  -> browser redirects to /thank-you
```

- `contact.html:215` — form POSTs directly to Web3Forms with the site access key. That is the entire funnel.
- `script.js:106` — after submit it also tries `POST /api/atlas-notify`, but: there is **no `api/` directory** in the website repo (404 on Vercel), the call is wrapped in `.catch(() => {})` (fails silently), and it only sends `{type, form_type, timestamp}` — **not name/email/phone**, so it could never populate a CRM even if it existed.
- **No Atlas endpoint receives website form submissions.** `atlas_brain/api/contacts.py` is read-only (timeline + call search).

**Net:** no real-time CRM write and no customer reply. Leads only reach the CRM via a delayed inbox-scraper (Area 1).

---

## Area 1 — Web form -> CRM lead: exists, but dormant / delayed / fragile / lossy

The only path that turns a submission into a CRM lead is an inbox-scraping background task, not a real-time hook.

- **Path:** `autonomous/tasks/gmail_digest.py` `_process_lead_emails` (304-369) reads inbox emails classified as `lead` and calls `crm.find_or_create_contact(source="web", contact_type="lead", tags=["web3forms"])` (343-350). `business_context_id` is **not** passed -> NULL.
- **Field loss:** `_parse_form_fields` (290-301) regex captures only `name|email|phone|message`. The form's **service, frequency, square-feet are silently dropped**; the logged message is truncated to 200 chars.
- **Classification is fragile:** `email_classifier.py` maps sender domain `web3forms.com -> lead` (line 81). The subject "New Estimate Request - Effingham Office Maids" matches **no** lead subject keyword (needs "new submission" / "contact form" / "website inquiry|lead|form"). A Gmail Promotions/Social auto-label can pre-empt classification.
- **Dormant by default:** master switch `autonomous.enabled` defaults **False** (`config.py:2045`; scheduler gated in `main.py:600`). Fast intake loop `email_intake.enabled` defaults **False** (`config.py:891`). IMAP creds blank by default.
- **Cadence:** default `gmail_digest` cron `5 7 * * *` = **07:05 America/Chicago, once daily** (`scheduler.py:351-364`). ~10 min only if `email_intake` is enabled (interval 600s). A lead at 8am can wait ~23h.
- **Preconditions to work at all:** `ATLAS_AUTONOMOUS_ENABLED=true`, an inbox reader (IMAP creds, or Gmail OAuth via `scripts/setup_google_oauth.py` in intake mode), Postgres up. Read query is `is:unread newer_than:1d`, 20-message cap — old/burst leads can be missed.
- **Customer reply: none.** No `email_provider.send` anywhere in this path. The only reaction is an optional operator **ntfy push** with a manual "Draft Reply" button, itself gated behind two default-off flags (`ntfy_enabled`, `email_draft.enabled`).

**Gaps:** off by default; drops service/frequency/sqft; classification hinges on the literal `web3forms.com` sender; NULL tenant; no customer acknowledgement; once/day latency by default.

---

## Area 2 — "Thank you / what to expect" email: transport ready, content piece missing

- **Send path works:** `services/email_provider.py` — `CompositeEmailProvider` (default from `get_email_provider()`): **Gmail preferred** (send + HTML), **Resend fallback** (send, **no HTML** — silently downgrades). `send(to, subject, body, from_email, reply_to, html, ...)`.
- **Config:** `EmailConfig` (`config.py:786`) — `enabled` defaults **False**; Gmail gated on OAuth token presence; Resend gated on `enabled + api_key`. **No dedicated From-name**; From defaults to the Gmail account or `ATLAS_EMAIL_DEFAULT_FROM`.
- **EOM branding already in code:** `templates/email/estimate_confirmation.py:8-28` — `BUSINESS_NAME`, `BUSINESS_PHONE="(217) 207-3097"`, `BUSINESS_EMAIL="info@effinghamofficemaids.com"`, website, address, terms, taglines. `info@...` is used as **reply-to** on `send_estimate`/`send_proposal`.
- **The blocking gap:** there is **no template/tool for a price-free, date-free request acknowledgement**. Every EOM template (`estimate_confirmation.py`, `proposal.py`) **requires a price and (for estimate) a scheduled date/time**, which don't exist at request time. `send_estimate` cannot be called without `service_date/service_time/price`. Only the untemplated `send_email` remains (would need an LLM to compose).
- **The richer EOM context** in `atlas_comms/core/config.py:241` (`_build_effingham_maids_context`: services, service area, pricing ranges, hours) is **not wired into any email path**.

**Data-hygiene bugs to fix when building the reply:**
- Stale phone `(217) 821-2370` in `skills/email/estimate_confirmation.md:44`, `cleaning_confirmation.md:46`, `proposal.md:43` — conflicts with the correct `(217) 207-3097` in the Python templates.
- Inconsistent street address across files: `503 S. 5th St` (`estimate_confirmation.py:9`) vs `1901 S. 4th St` (`proposal.py:10`, and the website footer).

---

## Area 3 — CRM schema vs EOM operational needs

Note: `contact_type`, `interaction_type`, `intent` are plain `VARCHAR` with **no DB constraint** — "allowed values" are comment conventions enforced only by calling code.

| Need | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Per-visit pricing** | ✅ Exists | `customer_services.rate NUMERIC(12,2)` + `rate_label DEFAULT 'Per Visit'` (`048_customer_services.sql:14-15`), keyed to `contact_id` (048:7); feeds `monthly_invoice_generation.py`. True standing rate. |
| **Scheduling** | 🟡 Partial | `appointments` (`012_appointments.sql:4-42`) has start/end, duration, status (confirmed/cancelled/completed/no_show), service_type, notes, `contact_id` (added 035:85-86). **No recurrence/frequency, no assigned cleaner, no per-visit price** (only `metadata JSONB`). Each visit is a discrete one-off row. |
| **Leads** | 🟡 Partial | `contacts.contact_type='lead'` (`035_contacts.sql:28`) works, but there is **no lead pipeline** — no stage/owner/next-follow-up fields. Nuance only via `tags`/`notes`/`metadata`. No dedicated leads table. |
| **Issues / complaints** | 🔴 Missing (dedicated) | No tickets/issues/complaints table for EOM customers. Only representable as a free-text `contact_interactions` row (`interaction_type='note', intent='complaint'`, e.g. `email_actions.py:118-123`). `contact_interactions` (035:67-76) has **no status/priority/assignee/resolution** columns. (052/053 complaint_* tables are consumer-review mining; 325/327 ticket_* are Content-Ops FAQ gen — not EOM customer service.) |

**Read scoping:** `search_contacts`/`list_contacts` apply a `business_context_id` filter **only when the caller passes it** (`crm_provider.py:270-273`, `354-357`); default is unscoped/all-tenant. `get_contact(id)` (239-241) has **no tenant filter at all**. Column + index exist (`idx_contacts_business_context`, 035:58-59) but nothing binds a default tenant.

---

## Area 4 — Existing-customer backfill + EOM-only tenant separation

**EOM context id:** literally `"effingham_maids"` (`atlas_comms/core/config.py:244`, registered 329-331).

**Which contact writers stamp `business_context_id`:**
- ✅ Stamp it: call intelligence (`call_intelligence.py:567`), SMS (`sms_intelligence.py:410`), SMS webhook fallback (`api/comms/webhooks.py:1545`).
- ❌ Leave NULL: booking (`tools/scheduling.py:427`), web-lead (`gmail_digest.py:343`), email backfill (`email_backfill.py:198`), calendar import (`scripts/import_calendar_contacts.py:492`), **B2B briefing gate** (`api/b2b_vendor_briefing.py:432`), **B2B campaign reply** (`autonomous/tasks/email_intake.py:613`).

**The B2B leak (confirmed):** `b2b_vendor_briefing.py:432` (churnsignals.co public gate) and `email_intake.py:613` (B2B campaign reply) both insert `contact_type='lead'` with **NULL** context into the **same** `contacts` table — software-sales leads mixing with cleaning customers on any unscoped read.

**Existing-customer data + import tooling:**
- Real booking history already lives in `appointments`, and it is **always tenant-stamped** (`012:24`, `business_context_id NOT NULL`; set at `scheduling.py:407`). Good backfill source of truth.
- `scripts/import_calendar_contacts.py` — reads **4 EOM Google Calendar ICS exports** (Commercial, Residential, One-Time, Estimates; machine-local paths under `/home/juan-canfield/PDF`), dedupes by address/phone/email, `create_contact(source="calendar_import")`, logs interactions. **Does not stamp `business_context_id`.**
- `autonomous/tasks/email_backfill.py` — Sent Mail (IMAP) -> `find_or_create_contact(source="email_backfill")`, idempotent by email. No context stamp.
- **Missing:** no appointments->contacts backfill (despite the documented `appointment_import` source), and no CSV importer.

**To achieve a clean "EOM-only" CRM, three changes + plug the leak:**
1. **Stamp writes** with `business_context_id="effingham_maids"` (booking, web-lead, email_backfill, calendar_import).
2. **Filter reads** — default/enforce `effingham_maids` at EOM callers + MCP `crm_server` (provider already supports it).
3. **Backfill existing NULL rows** (drive from tenant-stamped `appointments`, or `UPDATE contacts ... WHERE business_context_id IS NULL AND source IN (...)`). No such script exists.
4. **Stop the B2B leak** — give the two B2B writers their own context id (e.g. `churnsignals`) or route them to a separate table.

---

## Proposed work breakdown (for tracking — not yet started)

### Phase 0 — Instant reply now (no code)
- [ ] Enable the **Web3Forms Autoresponder** in the dashboard (From: Effingham Office Maids; "thanks, we'll reply within 24h"). Stopgap only — does not populate the CRM.

### Phase 1 — Immediate goal: real-time lead capture + branded acknowledgement
- [ ] Add an Atlas **lead-intake endpoint** (public, or via a Vercel serverless bridge) that receives the full form payload at submit time.
- [ ] Create/`find_or_create` the lead with **all fields** (name/email/phone/service/frequency/sqft/message) + `business_context_id="effingham_maids"` + `log_interaction`.
- [ ] Add a **request-acknowledgement email template** (price-free, date-free: "thanks for your request / here's what to expect / we reply within 24h") reusing EOM branding constants; send immediately via `email_provider`.
- [ ] Point `contact.html` / `script.js` at the new endpoint (replace/parallel the dead `/api/atlas-notify`).
- [ ] Fix the stale phone `(217) 821-2370` and the address inconsistency while touching email content.
- [ ] Decide reachability: public Atlas URL vs Vercel-function bridge (open decision below).

### Phase 2 — EOM-only tenant separation
- [ ] Stamp `effingham_maids` on the NULL-context writers (booking, web-lead, email_backfill, calendar_import).
- [ ] Default/enforce the `business_context_id` read filter for EOM surfaces.
- [ ] One-time backfill of existing NULL contact rows.
- [ ] Stop the B2B lead leak (`b2b_vendor_briefing.py:432`, `email_intake.py:613`).

### Phase 3 — Populate existing customers
- [ ] Choose the customer master source (Google Calendar ICS / CSV export / `appointments` history).
- [ ] Run/extend the importer **with** the tenant stamp; consider an appointments->contacts backfill.

### Phase 4 — Operational CRM depth
- [ ] Lead pipeline fields (stage / owner / next follow-up).
- [ ] Issues/complaints tracking (status / priority / assignee / resolution) — needs a dedicated structure.
- [ ] Recurring schedule + assigned cleaner + per-visit price on the appointment (or a clean link to `customer_services`).
- [ ] Later: T&C acceptance + Stripe card-on-file (Atlas already has a Stripe billing webhook in `api/billing.py`).

---

## Open decisions
1. **Lead reachability:** does Atlas have a public HTTPS URL (browser/Vercel can POST to), or do we add a Vercel serverless bridge (browser -> Vercel -> Atlas, shared secret)?
2. **Customer master for backfill:** the 4 Google Calendar ICS exports, a CSV export, or the `appointments` table already in Postgres?
3. **Lead capture approach:** true real-time intake at submit (root-cause fix, required for "reply the second they submit") vs. fixing/enabling the existing inbox-scraper path.

---
_Audit performed against code, not docs. File:line references are to `atlas_brain/` unless noted. Nothing in this issue has been implemented yet._

>
> The original body below says PR #292 is OPEN / DRAFT / UNMERGED and uses master `757fd17893c91f059db0f6427115ad77939d6e85`. That state is superseded: PR [#292](https://github.com/vahidmaghsoudi2/hbi/pull/292) merged at `a05e1708d24e2485c5f6307f8f85b2c676b6017d`. The issue's later management record [comment 6068607715](https://github.com/vahidmaghsoudi2/hbi/issues/293#issuecomment-6068607715) says WP-0 Reality Map = ACCEPTED / FROZEN, with implementation and contract changes not authorized.

>

>
# REC-V1 — Execution Plan & Work Split

## Objective
Move Recommendation V1 from repeated audit/reporting into controlled implementation, without restarting the work already completed.

## Current reality
- Current master: 757fd17893c91f059db0f6427115ad77939d6e85
- PR #292: a74a1f06ac264125437a17403afb517f5b076e4b
- PR #292 is OPEN / DRAFT / UNMERGED.
- CI #945 is GREEN on the PR SHA.
- Merge authorization: NOT AUTHORIZED.
- Contract changes: NOT AUTHORIZED.
- The PO-approved Recommendation V1 business decisions remain the authority.

## Execution rule
From this point, audits are no longer open-ended. Each member owns one closure/implementation stream and must return a decision-ready artifact. No duplicate generic audit.

## Work split

### Member 1 — Eligibility Path Owner
Close G-R1, G-R4, and G-R2 to the level necessary for implementation:
- legacy MatchScoringEngine / Final-Score eligibility active callers;
- approved Evidence Score versus broader Reasoning gates;
- reserved quantity semantics only insofar as Recommendation availability is affected.

Deliverable: concise evidence matrix, exact files/symbols/SHA/tests, final status, and minimal change proposal only if a concrete defect is proven.

### Member 2 — Contract & Acceptance Owner
Turn the locked Contract into an implementation checklist, specifically:
- §38 UI 5 + Show More on every active Recommendation entry path;
- AT-09 No Match semantics;
- §17 Explainability;
- §41–47 Ranking;
- Why / Why-Not;
- Selection vs Override;
- Fallback behavior.

Deliverable: prioritized acceptance checklist BLOCKING / REQUIRED / LATER, exact expected backend/UI behavior, no code.

### Member 3 — Integration / Red-Team Implementation Gate
Trace Candidate lifecycle:
A. never discovered
B. discovered but excluded
C. eligible but ranked lower

Verify both UI paths and identify the minimum changes needed to prevent silent conflation.

Deliverable: lifecycle table, proven gaps, minimal implementation scope, regression tests required.

## Manager / PO gate
After all three deliverables:
1. Manager consolidates one Decision Sheet.
2. PO authorizes exactly one implementation work package.
3. Implementation is performed only within that authorization.
4. Member 3 independently verifies the resulting diff and tests.
5. CI + runtime verification.
6. Acceptance.
7. Merge Authorization.

## Immediate implementation candidate
If the three streams confirm no higher-priority blocker:
REC-V1-UI-PARITY-§38
- align the active Home recommendation surface with locked §38;
- initial UI max 5;
- Show More for remaining eligible results;
- preserve backend full result set;
- preserve empty/fallback behavior;
- add/adjust tests;
- do not change ranking, eligibility, Evidence, or Contract semantics.

## Non-negotiable
KEEP → COMPLETE → CHANGE → BUILD.
No cleanup/refactor/rewrite merely for neatness.
No merge.
No new entity/model unless the business workflow proves it necessary.
No new Contract decision hidden inside implementation.

## Stage Ledger target
BASELINE / FACTS CONFIRMED / GAPS CLOSED / GAPS OPEN / CONTRACT IMPACT / IMPLEMENTATION IMPACT / NEXT AUTHORIZED ACTION.

items.title: PROGRAM: Waaiio prioritized execution backlog — release, security, product, and deferred work
items.body:
## Purpose

Maintain the single current priority order for Waaiio across release, security, product, UX, commercial, and deferred work so active items are not lost across chats/terminals.

This is a **program/tracking issue only**. It does not itself authorize implementation, merge, deployment, production DB mutation, provider calls, Meta template submission, or production E2E.

Repository/database/runtime evidence wins. Existing child issues/PRs remain the source of truth for their implementation details.

## Priority definitions

- **P0 — Production/release safety:** active production incompatibility, release gate, data/security integrity, or prerequisite blocking safe operation.
- **P1 — Pre-launch / launch-critical:** security or customer-visible functionality that should be resolved or explicitly accepted before broad production E2E/go-live.
- **P2 — Product/commercial next:** important product, onboarding, growth, finance, and UX work that can proceed after/alongside P0 without destabilizing the release gate.
- **P3 — Optimization / later:** useful improvements that are not current launch blockers.
- **DEFERRED:** intentionally postponed by owner/product decision.

---

# P0 — CURRENT RELEASE / PRODUCTION SAFETY

  - 355 history repaired; 356, 357, 360, 361, 362, 363, 364 applied and verified.
  - **Migration 359 remains blocked** because its `rolsuper=true` authority assumption is incompatible with Supabase Cloud production where `postgres` is non-superuser.
  - Next: repository-backed Phase A correction for 359; prove bootstrap + `save_commercial_config` + direct-write rejection + anon/non-admin bypass resistance under `rolsuper=false`; CTO review before implementation.
  - Production E2E remains separately unauthorized until #218 clears.

## MASTER-TRACKER COMPLETENESS RULE

Before beginning any substantive new Waaiio task:

1. Confirm the task is explicitly represented in #286 or a linked child issue.
2. If it is discovered in chat/audit and missing here, add it to #286 before implementation starts.
3. Update #286 when status changes to ACTIVE, BLOCKED, DONE/GREEN, or DEFERRED.
4. Never let a critical requirement, blocker, authorization boundary, or next step exist only in chat/terminal output.
5. Child issue/PR evidence always supersedes an older summary line in #286; update this tracker when the child state materially changes.

---

## Parallel-work policy

Work may proceed in parallel **only when it does not mutate the same production/release surface or create incompatible migrations**.

Recommended concurrency:

1. **Release lane:** #218 / production reconciliation until production DB/release compatibility is complete.
2. **Security lane:** #217, #287, #289 and related least-privilege work, isolated unless an explicit shared migration boundary is accepted.
3. **Active commercial lane:** #315 / PR #314 M378 until the design/implementation/release gate clears.
4. **Product lane:** #270 pricing/onboarding or #242 promo policy may be audited/decomposed in parallel, but no production-impacting merge bypasses the normal CTO/owner gate.
5. **Stale-PR lane:** audit #241/#240/#238/#120 one at a time and classify before reviving any code.

## Execution rule

For every item moved into active implementation:

1. Re-fetch current protected main and issue/PR state.
2. Phase A audit/blast radius where substantive.
3. Claude posts AGREE/PUSHBACK with evidence.
4. CTO architecture decision.
5. Isolated implementation + executable tests/CI.
6. CTO exact-head review.
7. Owner separately authorizes merge.
8. Deployment/production mutation/E2E remain separate gates where applicable.

## Mandatory task-governance protocol

Every substantive Waaiio task must be represented on this master tracker or on a linked child issue **before implementation begins**. Chat history is never the authoritative task list.

For each task/workstream, maintain a durable GitHub status using this visual model:

- ✅ **DONE / GREEN** — implementation and required completion gate are satisfied.
- 🟡 **ACTIVE** — currently being audited, designed, implemented, reviewed, or certified.
- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot safely proceed until a named dependency/correction/authorization is resolved.
- ⬜ **QUEUED** — known work, not yet active.
- ⚪ **DEFERRED** — intentionally postponed by owner/product decision.

### Required documentation checkpoints

For every active task, GitHub must record:

1. **Problem / objective** — what user/business/technical problem is being solved.
2. **Current evidence** — exact protected-main SHA plus repo/DB/runtime evidence that establishes the starting state.
3. **Dependencies / blast radius** — all affected application surfaces, including where relevant:
   - customer-facing app/web flows,
   - WhatsApp/bot runtime,
   - Admin application,
   - Supabase schema/RLS/RPCs/migrations,
   - payment/provider integrations,
   - background/recovery jobs,
   - reporting/finance/analytics,
   - shared-number / tenant-isolation behavior,
   - deployment/runtime configuration.
4. **Claude implementation proposal** — exact architecture, files/surfaces expected to change, migration/data impact, failure behavior, security/financial implications, and executable test strategy.
5. **CTO independent review** — ChatGPT verifies the proposal against current repository/database/runtime evidence and explicitly AGREEs, REVISEs, or PUSHBACKs.
6. **Substantive agreement before coding** — Claude must explicitly AGREE or PUSHBACK on the CTO architecture/refinements. Any disagreement is resolved on GitHub before implementation starts.
7. **Definition of Done before coding** — acceptance criteria must be explicit and testable. Green CI alone is never sufficient for security, payments, migrations, concurrency, authorization, financial state, or cross-tenant work.
8. **Implementation evidence** — branch, base SHA, exact head SHA, changed surfaces, executable tests, DB/runtime proofs, and CI.
9. **CTO exact-head gate** — ChatGPT independently reviews the exact PR head and returns READY FOR MERGE or BLOCKED.
10. **Owner merge authorization** — required separately after CTO readiness.
11. **Production/deployment/E2E gate** — separately authorized where applicable; merge never implies deployment, provider action, DB mutation, or production E2E.
12. **Master-board update** — update #286 status when the task becomes ACTIVE, BLOCKED, DONE, DEFERRED, or changes priority. Do this before moving to the next task.

### Definition of Done rule

A task is not ✅ DONE merely because code was merged. Its Definition of Done must account for the task's real completion boundary, which may include schema reconciliation, Admin UI behavior, bot/runtime behavior, provider/template readiness, production verification, observability, rollback/recovery proof, documentation, and/or E2E certification.

### Dependency rule

Do not review a change in isolation when it crosses application boundaries. For substantive work, explicitly audit neighboring callers/consumers and ensure the **main app + Admin + database/runtime + bot/provider paths remain compositionally compatible**. If one surface depends on another migration, deployment, configuration, or provider state, that dependency must be named and gated.

### Update discipline

Before starting the next priority item, confirm the current task's GitHub issue/PR and #286 have been updated with the latest authoritative state. If a task is discovered in chat or during an audit and is not represented on GitHub, capture it on #286 (or create/link a child issue) before proceeding.

Dependencies are allowed. File/schema collisions are not.

5. No Lane 3 task may broaden into channel routing, shared-number allocation, localization corpus/certification, onboarding, or #266 architecture.

items.title: V6: Direct Sale Import — import off-platform ticket sales from CSV/Excel

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Spec complete; safe for an agent to implement

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Event organizers sell a meaningful share of their tickets **themselves, off-platform** — for cash at a rehearsal, by bank transfer to a friend, at a stall with no card reader. Today those sales live only in the organizer's head or a spreadsheet. Ticket POS has no way to record them, so:

- **Capacity is wrong.** The system thinks seats are available that were already sold, so the Storefront can oversell.
- **There is no unified view.** Staff can't see true sold/remaining numbers because a whole channel is missing.
- **Buyers of those tickets get nothing** — no confirmation, no record they can show at the door.

Organizers need to hand the system a list of the sales they already made and have it become real, capacity-correct sales — without hand-typing each one and without silently corrupting their catalog.

## Solution

A **Direct Sale Import** on each Event: the organizer downloads a per-event spreadsheet template, fills in the sales they made, uploads it, reviews a full validation **preview**, and confirms. Each row becomes a recorded **Ticket Sale** on the `import` channel with source `direct`, decrementing Ticket Type capacity exactly as an online or in-person sale would, and emailing each buyer a **Sale Confirmation**. Mistakes are recoverable: the **latest** import on an Event can be undone, restoring capacity and optionally notifying affected buyers.

Because no sales pipeline exists yet, this feature also builds the **shared sales spine** (`ticket_sales`, `ticket_sale_lines`, atomic capacity decrement, the Sale Confirmation artifact, and an `EmailSender` boundary) that online sales and the Integration Partner API will later reuse.

## User Stories

**Recording direct sales**

1. As an event organizer, I want to download a spreadsheet template for a specific Event, so that I fill in sales against that Event's real Ticket Types without guessing names or IDs.
2. As an event organizer, I want the template to pre-list my Event's Ticket Types as a locked dropdown, so that I can't fat-finger a type name and have rows silently mismatch.
3. As an event organizer, I want to record, per sale, the buyer's email and name, the Ticket Type, quantity, payment method, and date, so that the sale is complete and the buyer is reachable.
4. As an event organizer, I want to mark whether each sale was paid by cash or bank transfer, so that my records reflect how the money actually came in.
5. As an event organizer, I want to optionally record the amount I actually charged per ticket, so that comps and friend-discounts aren't misreported as full price.
6. As an event organizer, I want a blank amount to default to the catalog price, so that I only type an amount when it differs.
7. As an event organizer, I want to upload either a `.csv` or an `.xlsx` file, so that I can use whichever my spreadsheet tool produces.
8. As an event organizer, I want each imported sale to count against the Ticket Type's remaining capacity, so that my Storefront stops overselling seats I already sold.

**Preview and validation**

9. As an event organizer, I want a preview of every parsed row before anything is saved, so that I can trust what I'm about to record.
10. As an event organizer, I want **all** problems in my file surfaced at once, not one at a time, so that I can fix everything in a single edit-and-re-upload cycle.
11. As an event organizer, I want rows with an unknown Ticket Type, a malformed email, a missing required field, or a future sale date flagged clearly, so that I know exactly what to correct.
12. As an event organizer, I want to be warned when a row looks like a sale I already imported (same email, type, and date), so that I don't double-count — while still being able to keep it if the buyer genuinely bought again.
13. As an event organizer, I want to skip or keep each flagged possible-duplicate individually, so that repeat buyers and accidental re-uploads are handled correctly.
14. As an event organizer, I want to see the capacity impact of the import in the preview ("GA will be 95/100"), so that I understand the effect before committing.
15. As an event organizer, I want to be blocked from committing an import that would exceed a Ticket Type's capacity, so that the system never records more sold than exists.
16. As an event organizer, when an import would oversell, I want an inline action to raise that Ticket Type's capacity to fit, so that I can record sales that really happened without leaving the flow.
17. As an event organizer, I want the confirm step to tell me how many sales I'm about to create, so that the scale of the action is unmistakable.

**Commit, confirmations, and idempotency**

18. As an event organizer, I want the whole import to succeed or fail as one unit, so that I never end up with a half-recorded batch.
19. As an event organizer, I want a double-click or network retry on submit to be a safe no-op, so that I don't accidentally post the batch twice.
20. As a buyer of a direct sale, I want to receive a Sale Confirmation email with a reference code, so that I have proof of my purchase to show at the door.
21. As an event organizer, I want every buyer in a committed import to be emailed their confirmation automatically, so that direct sales are handled the same as online sales.

**History and undo**

22. As an event organizer, I want a per-Event history of imports (when, how many sales, by whom), so that I can see what's been recorded and spot an accidental re-upload.
23. As an event organizer, I want to undo the most recent import on an Event, so that I can walk back a wrong-file or wrong-event mistake.
24. As an event organizer, when I undo an import, I want the sales removed and capacity restored, so that the Event's numbers return to exactly what they were.
25. As an event organizer, I want to choose whether undoing notifies affected buyers that their confirmation is cancelled, so that I don't spam people over a mistake they never saw, but can correct the record when they did.

**Access**

26. As an Org Admin, I want to run and undo imports on any of my Organization's Events, so that I can manage sales across the org.
27. As a Member who can manage an Event's sales, I want import and undo gated by that same permission, so that access widens automatically to Event Owners and assigned Event Staff when roles ship (V7) without a rework.

## Implementation Decisions

### Scope: build the shared sales spine, delivered via import

`internal/sales` is currently package stubs. This slice builds the sales core that all channels share, exercised end-to-end by the import feature. Delivered in three stages (see Further Notes):

- **Sales core** — `ticket_sales` and `ticket_sale_lines`, a record-sale service that inserts a sale + lines and **atomically decrements `ticket_types.sold_count`** under row locks (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), and the `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` domain error. (Pulls roadmap D1–D5 forward.)
- **Sale Confirmation** — a new per-sale artifact with a human-readable reference code (e.g. `TP-3F9K2`), emitted whenever a Ticket Sale is recorded.
- **`EmailSender` boundary** — an interface with a dev/log sink implementation now; the harness already provides a capture double. A real provider is deferred to V9. Import and future online sales share this path.

### Domain model (already updated in `CONTEXT.md`)

- **Sales Channel** enum: `online | in_person | import`.
- **Sales Source** (imports only): `external_platform | direct`. This slice builds `direct`.
- **Direct Sale**: a Ticket Sale the org made off-platform, carrying a **Payment Method** (`cash | transfer` at launch; modeled as an extensible set).
- **Sale Confirmation**: per-sale receipt + reference code, emailed to the Customer. Not a per-attendee admission ticket; schema leaves room to attach individual tickets later.
- **Customer**: now identified by a required email and name on every Ticket Sale.

### Schema

- **`ticket_sales`**: `id`, `event_id`, `organization_id`, `channel`, `source` (nullable; set when `channel = import`), `payment_method` (nullable; set when `source = direct`), buyer `email` (required), buyer `name` (required), `sold_at`, `import_batch_id` (nullable FK), `idempotency_key`, `confirmation_ref`, `status` (active/reversed), timestamps.
- **`ticket_sale_lines`**: `id`, `ticket_sale_id`, `ticket_type_id`, `quantity`, `unit_price_cents` (**snapshot** at sale time — from the file's amount if present, else the current catalog price; `0` = comp).
- **`sale_import_batches`**: `id`, `event_id`, `organization_id`, `source`, actor member id, row/sale counts, `status` (committed/reversed), `created_at`. Powers history, undo, and duplicate visibility.
- **Mapping rule**: **1 file row = 1 Ticket Sale = 1 Ticket Sale Line.** Grouping multiple lines into one sale via an optional `order_ref` column is deferred (schema should not preclude it).
- **Invariant**: `sold_count ≤ capacity` holds at all times. Import never breaks it; oversell is blocked, not clamped.

### File format & template

- **Both `.csv` and `.xlsx` are parsed server-side in Go** (add an xlsx library such as `excelize`). Uploading the raw file keeps one authoritative parse/validate/commit core that external-platform CSVs and the Integration Partner API (V8) can reuse. **Update the "CSV only" note in `technical-design.md`.**
- **Per-event template** (`.xlsx`) is generated server-side, pre-listing the Event's Ticket Types with a **locked dropdown** and the internal `ticket_type_id` in a hidden/reference column, so the organizer fills blanks rather than typing type names.
- **Columns**: `email*`, `name*`, `ticket_type*`, `quantity*`, `payment_method*` (dropdown `cash|transfer`), `sold_at*` (ISO-8601; Excel date cells coerced; interpreted in the **Event timezone**), `amount?` (unit price; blank → catalog price). `*` = required.
- A reasonable row limit applies (target ~10,000 rows per batch).

### API contract (Staff routes)

Three staff endpoints behind the Staff BFF, all scoped to an Event and gated by `can_manage_event_sales(member, event)`:

- **Template download** — returns the pre-filled per-event `.xlsx`.
- **Preview** — accepts the uploaded file, parses and validates **every** row server-side, and returns a per-row result set: matched Ticket Type, field errors, future-date errors, capacity/oversell status per Ticket Type, and **soft duplicate flags** (row matches an existing active sale on `email + ticket_type + sold_at` date). No writes. Response also carries the computed capacity impact per Ticket Type and the total sale count.
- **Commit** — accepts the reviewed file/rows plus per-row skip decisions and a client-generated **idempotency key**; runs as a **single transaction**: re-validate under row locks, insert sales + lines, decrement capacity, create the `sale_import_batches` record, emit a Sale Confirmation per sale. All-or-nothing: any oversell (e.g. a capacity race lost since preview) fails the whole batch with `IMPORT_BATCH_FAILED` (details carry the first offending Ticket Type / row) and the client re-previews. A replayed idempotency key returns the original result without re-committing.
- **Undo** — reverses the **latest** committed batch on the Event only: marks its sales `reversed`, restores `sold_count`, marks the batch `reversed`, and — **only if the caller sets `notify_buyers`** — sends a void/cancellation email to each affected buyer via the same `EmailSender`. Silent otherwise.

All responses use the standard `{ data, error, request_id }` envelope and existing error-code conventions (see the api-errors skill).

### Duplicate handling

Email is a **soft signal, never a unique key** (repeat buyers are legitimate). Protection is two-layered: a **batch idempotency key** (double-submit/retry safety) plus **per-row match flags** in the preview that the organizer resolves as skip/keep. No content-hash file blocking at launch.

### Oversell handling

Blocked, not absorbed. Preview reports the overage per Ticket Type; the organizer either trims rows or uses the inline **raise-capacity** action (a normal catalog edit on that Ticket Type) and re-previews. This preserves `sold_count ≤ capacity` everywhere and keeps capacity truthful for concurrent online/in-person sales.

### Email behavior

- **Commit always emails** each buyer their Sale Confirmation (parity with online sales; dev sink now, real at V9).
- **Undo emails only when `notify_buyers` is set.** Asymmetry is intentional (organizer decides at cancel time). Noted for review.

### Information architecture (Staff app)

- Import lives **on the Event** (Event detail → an "Import sales" surface): download template → upload → preview → confirm → history → undo.
- **Per-event import history** is shown there.
- The existing global `/imports` placeholder becomes an **event picker** that routes into the per-event flow.
- The Staff Next.js app proxies these calls to the Go API through its BFF, consistent with existing staff routes.

### Permissions

Both import and undo are gated by `can_manage_event_sales(member, event)` — Org Admin today (the only live role); Event Owner and assigned Event Staff inherit it automatically once V7 lands. No import-specific role logic.

## Testing Decisions

**What makes a good test here:** assert external, user-visible behavior — HTTP status, the `{ data, error, request_id }` envelope, `error.code`, resulting **remaining capacity**, the preview's per-row verdicts, and **captured emails** — never internal function shapes. Follow `docs/testing.md`.

- **Primary seam — HTTP integration (`backend/integration/`).** Add `sales_test.go` and `import_test.go`. Exercise the real staff routes request-in/response-out, covering: template download shape; preview surfacing *all* row errors at once; unknown-type / bad-email / missing-field / future-date flagging; soft duplicate flags with skip vs keep; oversell blocked with `IMPORT_BATCH_FAILED` and the raise-capacity path unblocking it; successful commit decrementing capacity and producing correct sales/lines with price snapshots (including `0` comps); confirmation emails captured on commit; idempotency-key replay returning the original result; undo restoring capacity, and void emails present only when `notify_buyers` is set. Prior art: `catalog_test.go`, `auth_test.go`, and the harness's capture email sender + fixed clock.
- **Repository exception (`internal/sales/repository/`), narrowly.** Only concurrency/locking the docs already sanction: atomic capacity decrement under concurrent sales, all-or-nothing rollback when a batch races another sale into oversell, and idempotency replay races. Each **must** be paired with an HTTP test proving the user-visible outcome.
- **Out of the test scope:** no new Staff Playwright suite (per `docs/testing.md`, Playwright is reserved for storefront-only UI behavior and thin cross-runtime E2E smoke). A single thin import→capacity E2E smoke may be added later under `e2e/` (roadmap J5) but is not required by this spec.

## Out of Scope

- **`external_platform` source** — the original Eventbrite-style Sale Import. This slice ships `direct` only; the schema and pipeline are built to accommodate it later.
- **Per-attendee admission tickets / QR codes / door scanning.** The artifact is a per-sale Sale Confirmation; individual tickets attach later.
- **A real email provider** (vendor, DKIM, deliverability, templates) — deferred to V9. This slice builds the boundary + dev sink only.
- **Online checkout (V5)** and **Integration Partner API (V8)** — they reuse this spine but are not built here.
- **Grouping multiple lines into one Ticket Sale** via `order_ref`.
- **Reversing any batch other than the latest**, and partial-batch reversal.
- **Content-hash duplicate-file blocking.**
- **`payment_method` values beyond `cash|transfer`** (the enum is extensible but no other values validate now).
- **Event Owner / Event Staff role plumbing (V7)** — the permission gate is written to widen automatically, but the roles themselves land in V7.

## Further Notes

**Recommended staging** (all within this one issue; each stage is independently reviewable):

- **Stage 1 — Sales spine + confirmation email.** `ticket_sales` / `ticket_sale_lines` schema, record-sale service with atomic capacity decrement + `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, Sale Confirmation artifact, `EmailSender` boundary + dev sink. Proven by HTTP + repository concurrency tests. Nothing user-facing yet, but it's the reusable core.
- **Stage 2 — Import pipeline + Staff UI.** `sale_import_batches`, server-side `.csv`/`.xlsx` parsing, per-event template generation, preview (all-errors + soft duplicate flags + oversell/raise-capacity), all-or-nothing commit with idempotency, confirmation emails, per-event history, and the Event "Import sales" UI (global `/imports` → event picker).
- **Stage 3 — Undo.** Latest-batch reversal, capacity restore, and the opt-in void-email path (reused by future refunds).

**Scope consequence:** this deliberately pulls roadmap D1–D5 (sales core) and a slice of V9 (email boundary) forward, because "email parity + build the core" requires the shared spine to exist. This is the intended architecture, not scope creep — the spine is built once and reused by V5 and V8.

**Asymmetry flagged for reviewers:** committing an import always emails buyers; undoing only emails when the organizer opts in. Once real email is live (V9), a wrong-file import will have genuinely emailed those buyers, and undo permits not notifying them — the import confirm step is the intended safeguard.

**Docs to update alongside code:** `technical-design.md` (Sale Import: broaden beyond External Platform, add `source`, note `.xlsx` server-side parsing), `roadmap.md` (V6 / sections D + G status), and the already-updated `CONTEXT.md`.

items.title: KB Ingestion Phase 3: Cloud Deployment Guide + Worked Examples
items.body:
## Context

Phase 3 sub-ticket of Epic [#11624](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11624) (Cloud-Native KB Ingestion for External Workspaces). Graduated from [Discussion #11623](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/11623). **Blocked-by Phase 2 #11626** — guide content depends on stable Phase 0/1 contracts AND Phase 2 service+facade shape (operator and ingestion-flow examples need real endpoint names + payload shapes to be substrate-correct).

This phase ships the **operator-facing substrate** for self-service cloud Agent OS deployments: a guide tree explaining how clients configure KB, write custom sources/parsers, wire git hooks, and reason about tenant boundaries.

## The Problem

After Phase 0/1 + Phase 2 land, the system is technically functional for cloud deployments — but cloud operators have no documented onboarding path. Per Discussion #11623 §9 + operator framing:

> *"a graduation goal for the sandbox epic must include a new guide, which explains how clients can configure KB and their deployment pipelines."*

Without the guide:
- Cloud deployment teams must reverse-engineer the contracts from source code
- Custom-source/custom-parser authoring becomes word-of-mouth knowledge
- Hook-wiring + tenant-boundary semantics get re-derived per deployment
- Security boundaries (operator-installed/Neo-shipped/signed-package for server-side parsers; client-side for everything else) lack a canonical reference

## The Architectural Reality

This phase creates a new guide tree:

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Overview.md` | What cloud-deployed Agent OS is; how ingestion topology works; the contract-split + facade pattern; relationship to Neo's curated content |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Configuration.md` | `useDefaultSources` / `useDefaultParsers` / `customSources` / `customParsers` / tenant config storage shape |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/CustomSources.md` | Authoring a custom Source class (extending `Base.extract`), registering it, path conventions, identity-tuple semantics |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/CustomParsers.md` | Authoring a custom Parser (server-side OR client-side), `parsed-chunk-v1` contract, parser-protocol JSON Schema usage, non-JS parser distribution patterns |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/HookWiring.md` | Git hook examples (pre-push, post-commit); `ingestSourceFiles` MCP tool usage; bulk-facade for large initial imports; batch sizing; tombstone payload shape; revision-boundary reconciliation |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Security.md` | Parser-execution boundaries; tenant isolation invariants; auth flow; untrusted-code policy; write-side stamping + spoof-rejection invariants; **KB-as-cache vs MC-as-store data-recovery framing** (KB wipes are always recoverable from external sources via tenant re-push or `npm run ai:sync-kb`; MC wipes have an amnesia window minimized by daily backup daemon — plan retention accordingly per Phase 4 Epic [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) framing) |
| **NEW** `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/MigrationPath.md` | How existing Neo deployments upgrade to v13 with zero-config (default inheritance); breaking changes; deprecation timeline |
| **NEW** `examples/cloud-deployment/minimal-external-workspace/` | Working example external workspace with one custom source + one custom parser |
| **NEW** `examples/cloud-deployment/pre-push-hook.sh` | Minimal shell `pre-push` hook demonstrating `ingestSourceFiles` contract |

## The Fix

### 1. Guide Tree Authoring

Each `*.md` document follows existing `learn/agentos/` discipline:
- Anchor & Echo discipline (per AGENTS.md): JSDoc `@summary` cross-links to relevant source files
- Cross-links to #9999, #10010, #10011, #10030 for retrieval-side / identity / RLS / concept-ontology substrate
- Cross-links to Phase 0/1 (#11625) + Phase 2 (#TBD) schemas + service contracts
- Capability framing only (no commercial-customer references; per Neo's external-positioning discipline)

### 2. Worked Example

`examples/cloud-deployment/minimal-external-workspace/`:
- Minimal `package.json` (Neo as dependency)
- One source file in a hypothetical language (e.g., `.proto` for protobuf — common cross-language demo)
- One custom Source class registered via the Phase 0/1 registry API
- One custom Parser emitting `parsed-chunk-v1` records
- README explaining how to run the example end-to-end

### 3. Hook Example

`examples/cloud-deployment/pre-push-hook.sh`:
- Bash `pre-push` hook
- Computes `git diff` against last-pushed SHA
- Calls `ingestSourceFiles` via the bulk-facade CLI (or MCP tool depending on batch size)
- Handles delete tombstones + revision-boundary payload
- Comments explain extension points for client customization

### 4. Validation

- All referenced files in guide examples actually exist
- All code examples are runnable (CI lint or manual smoke test)
- All cross-references resolve (no dead `#NNNN` or `[link]` references)
- Guide tree integrates into `learn/tree.json` discovery

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Overview.md` written and linked in `learn/tree.json`
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Configuration.md` written; documents all configs introduced in Phase 0/1 + Phase 2
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/CustomSources.md` written; includes worked-example reference
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/CustomParsers.md` written; covers server-side AND client-side parser authoring
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/HookWiring.md` written; includes shell-hook example reference
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Security.md` written; codifies write-side stamping + spoof-rejection + parser sandboxing boundaries + KB-as-cache vs MC-as-store data-recovery framing (cross-link to Phase 4 Epic #11628 retention-policy framing)
- [ ] `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/MigrationPath.md` written; documents zero-config upgrade path for existing Neo deployments
- [ ] `examples/cloud-deployment/minimal-external-workspace/` exists and runs end-to-end
- [ ] `examples/cloud-deployment/pre-push-hook.sh` exists and demonstrates the contract
- [ ] All guide-referenced files exist (validation step)
- [ ] All code examples runnable (manual smoke test documented in PR)
- [ ] Guide tree appears in KB after `manage_knowledge_base({action: 'sync'})` — `learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/*.md` chunked + retrievable

## Out of Scope

- Generated API docs from inline JSDoc (handled by existing `docs/` build pipeline)
- Per-client deployment runbooks (those belong to client-side documentation, not Neo substrate)
- Marketing or commercial-positioning material (capability framing only — neutral technical reference)
- WASM/tree-sitter server-side parser sandboxing patterns → future Discussion when feature exists

## Avoided Traps

| Trap | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Writing the guide before Phase 2 stabilizes | Endpoint names / payload shapes can drift; guide examples become stale before they ship |
| Skipping the worked example | Configuration docs without runnable examples are unverifiable; future agents/operators re-derive |
| Skipping `learn/tree.json` integration | Guide invisible to KB sync → invisible to agents using `ask_knowledge_base` for cloud-deployment queries |
| Generic / aspirational language | Capability framing requires precision; vague "supports custom parsers" loses to "register parser ID + config via `aiConfig.knowledgeBase.customParsers`" |
| Marketing tone | Neo's guide voice is reference-technical, not commercial-promotional |

## Related

- **Parent Epic:** [#11624](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11624)
- **Blocked-by:** Phase 2 #11626 (service + facade shape must stabilize) — itself blocked-by Phase 0/1 [#11625]
- **Origin Discussion:** #11623 (§9 Guide Deliverable specifies the tree)
- **Cross-substrate guide siblings:** `learn/agentos/KnowledgeBase.md`, `learn/agentos/tooling/MultiTenantMigrationGuide.md`, `learn/agentos/CodeExecution.md`, `learn/agentos/SharedDeployment.md`

## Origin Session ID

`7360e917-1733-4cdd-a6f3-5ac51c34b838`

## Handoff Retrieval Hints

- `query_raw_memories({query: 'cloud deployment guide custom sources parsers hook wiring'})`
- `ask_knowledge_base({query: 'learn agentos guide tree structure new substrate', type: 'guide'})`
- Discussion #11623 §9 is the authoritative scope-source
- Phase 2 (#TBD) MUST be merged before drafting `HookWiring.md` + worked example (depends on real endpoint names + payload shapes)
- Sections that CAN be drafted post-Phase-0/1, pre-Phase-2 (low-risk): `Overview.md` (architectural framing), `Security.md` (sandboxing + write-side stamping invariants), `MigrationPath.md` (zero-config upgrade story). Saves wall-clock time if Phase 3 starts in parallel once Phase 0/1 merges.

items.title: Saved card replacement — audit + design
items.body:
## Saved Card Replacement — Phase 1 Audit + Design

### Requirement

A customer who pays with a NEW reusable Paystack card can replace their existing saved card for that business without manually typing \`remove card\` first.

---

### 1. Current Save-Card / Saved-Card Reuse Call Graph

\`\`\`
"save card" command
  → global-queries.ts isSaveCardQuery()
  → saved-cards.ts handleSaveCard()
    → finds latest paid booking/payment
